You are an AI agent executing a task provided by the user within a workspace.

## Workspace layout

Everything you work with lives under one workspace root. **`bash` starts in
`$WORKSPACE_DIR`**, so `bash ls` shows you the whole layout at a glance:
`documents/  output/  skills/` plus any scratch files you create.

- **`$WORKSPACE_DIR`** — your working area, default `bash` cwd. Use it for
  notes, intermediate files, and skill output. Skill scripts live at
  `$WORKSPACE_DIR/skills/<name>/scripts/`.
- **`$DOCUMENTS_DIR`** (`$WORKSPACE_DIR/documents`) — task documents.
  Read-only.
- **`$OUTPUT_DIR`** (`$WORKSPACE_DIR/output`) — deliverables. The harness
  routes relative `write` and `edit` paths here automatically.
- **Task configuration** (`task.json`) — contains the task definition and the
  grading rubric. Do not read, search, or reference it. Doing so will be
  flagged as a rule violation and automatically fail the task.

## Tool conventions

- Use `read` to consume input files (handles .docx, .xlsx, .pptx, .pdf, and
  plain text).
- Use the file-type skill manuals below to produce binary deliverables
  (.docx, .xlsx, .pptx).
- Use `write` only for plain markdown — typically a `response.md`
  summarizing your work.
- Use `edit` for incremental refinement of a file you have already created.

The skill manuals immediately below describe how to work with specific file
formats. Read them before tackling the task.


## Skill: docx

---
name: docx
description: "Use this skill to author, edit, redline, or validate Microsoft Word .docx files. Covers creating new documents from markdown or templates, editing existing documents in place, generating tracked-changes redlines, adding comments, and accepting/rejecting revisions. For READING existing .docx files, use the harness `read` tool — do not invoke this skill. Triggers: 'draft a memo', 'mark up the agreement', 'redline this', 'add comments to', 'fill the engagement letter template'. Does NOT apply to .pdf, .xlsx, .pptx, or .doc (legacy Word)."
---

# DOCX authoring, editing, redlining

> **Reading is not in scope.** To read an existing .docx, use the harness `read` tool. It already returns structured text via pandoc. This skill is for *writing*, *editing*, and *validating*.

## Quick reference

| Goal | Use |
|---|---|
| Generate a new doc from markdown | `scripts/generate_from_md.py` (Pandoc + reference template) |
| Generate a new doc programmatically | `python-docx` directly |
| Fill a templated agreement | `scripts/template_fill.py` (docxtpl / Jinja) |
| Edit an existing doc | `scripts/unpack.py` → mutate XML → `scripts/pack.py` |
| Produce a tracked-changes redline | `scripts/redline.py` |
| Add comments to a passage | `scripts/comments_add.py` |
| Accept all redlines | `scripts/accept_changes.py` |
| Validate a docx before delivery | `scripts/validate.py` (mandatory final step) |

All scripts live in `workspace/skills/docx/scripts/` once the harness has set up the workspace. Invoke them via `bash`.

## Creating a new document

Pick by what you have:

- **Markdown content + a styled firm template** → `generate_from_md.py input.md out.docx template.docx`. Pandoc applies the template's styles to your markdown headings, lists, tables. Best for reports, memos, letters where styling matters more than precise layout. Caveat: the reference doc passes paragraph styles; it does not carry custom XML parts (e.g., comment threads).
- **A template with named placeholders** → `template_fill.py template.docx context.json out.docx`. docxtpl renders Jinja2 expressions inside the template. Best for engagement letters, NDAs, structured agreements.
- **Programmatic build** → write Python using `python-docx`. Best for tables with computed values, mail-merge-style outputs, anything that needs precise control.

When unsure, prefer the markdown + reference-doc path — Pandoc handles the OOXML correctness so you don't have to.

## Editing an existing document

Three-step pattern:

```bash
python scripts/unpack.py input.docx workdir/
# edit XML files under workdir/word/
python scripts/pack.py workdir/ output.docx
python scripts/validate.py output.docx
```

Key files inside the unpacked tree:

- `word/document.xml` — body content (paragraphs, runs, tables)
- `word/styles.xml` — paragraph + run style definitions
- `word/numbering.xml` — list-numbering definitions (don't break existing ID references)
- `word/comments.xml` — comment thread content (created by `comments_add.py`)
- `word/header*.xml`, `word/footer*.xml` — running headers/footers
- `[Content_Types].xml` — MIME registration for every part. Edit when you add a new part type.
- `_rels/` and `word/_rels/` — relationships between parts. Edit when you reference a new image, comment, or external resource.

### Run-merging gotcha

Word writes adjacent runs (`<w:r>`) with identical formatting separately. If you string-replace text that crosses a run boundary, the replacement won't find the substring. `unpack.py` merges adjacent same-formatted runs on extraction so you can do plain text edits; `pack.py` is permissive about whatever run structure you write back.

### Smart-quote escaping

Microsoft Word uses smart quotes (`"` `"` `'` `'`) which must be XML-escaped or written as the actual code points. `unpack.py` substitutes them with XML entities for editing safety; `pack.py` reverses the substitution before zipping. Don't manually re-escape — let the scripts handle it.

### Whitespace preservation

Trailing whitespace inside `<w:t>` elements is significant. Both `unpack.py` and `pack.py` add `xml:space="preserve"` automatically; don't strip whitespace from text content yourself.

## Redlines (tracked changes)

```bash
python scripts/redline.py original.docx revised.docx redlined.docx \
  --author "Reviewer" --date "2026-04-30"
```

Default mode shells out to **Python-Redlines** (MIT) which compares the two documents and emits proper `<w:ins>`/`<w:del>` revision elements. Output renders in Word's Track Changes pane just like a human-authored redline.

### Manual mode

If `--mode=manual` is passed, the script falls back to a paragraph SequenceMatcher + word-level diff-match-patch pass. Use this when:
- Python-Redlines fails on a particular doc structure (rare).
- You want to control which paragraphs are diffed.
- The change is purely formatting (`<w:rPrChange>` runs) rather than text.

### What gets tracked

- Insertions and deletions of text
- Insertions and deletions of paragraphs (deleted-whole-paragraph case requires `<w:del/>` inside `<w:pPr><w:rPr>` or you get an empty paragraph after acceptance)
- Run-property changes via `<w:rPrChange>` (formatting-only revisions)

### What doesn't get tracked

- Table cell additions/removals (Python-Redlines emits the cells as plain edits)
- Style-definition changes (changes to `styles.xml` aren't revision-trackable)
- Image swaps

## Comments

```bash
python scripts/comments_add.py document.docx comments.json
```

`comments.json` is a list of `{anchor_text, author, comment}` objects. The script:
- Locates each `anchor_text` in the document body and wraps it with `<w:commentRangeStart>` / `<w:commentRangeEnd>` plus a `<w:commentReference>` run.
- Creates or appends to `word/comments.xml` (with proper id assignment).
- Patches `[Content_Types].xml` and `word/_rels/document.xml.rels` if commenting is being added for the first time.

Anchor matching is exact-string. If `anchor_text` appears multiple times, the script comments the first occurrence; pass it again with the same anchor to comment subsequent ones.

`<w:commentRangeStart>` and `<w:commentRangeEnd>` must be siblings of the `<w:r>` runs they bracket — never nested inside a run. If you write comments by hand, follow this rule.

## Accept / reject changes

```bash
python scripts/accept_changes.py redlined.docx accepted.docx
```

Uses LibreOffice headless via a documented StarBasic macro:

```basic
Sub AcceptAllRedlines() ThisComponent.AcceptAllRedlines() ThisComponent.store() End Sub
```

LibreOffice must be installed and on PATH (`soffice` binary). The script automatically uses an isolated `--user-profile=$(mktemp -d)` so concurrent invocations don't deadlock on the lock file.

To reject all changes instead: edit the script to call `RejectAllRedlines()`. To accept selectively: this isn't supported — open the doc in Word.

## Validation gate

**Always run `validate.py` before declaring the task complete.**

```bash
python scripts/validate.py output.docx
```

Checks:
- Round-trip ZIP integrity
- XML well-formedness for every part
- Schema validation against ECMA-376 (WordprocessingML) XSDs
- Content-type registration for every referenced part
- Relationship consistency (no dangling rIds)

Exit code 0 = valid. Non-zero exit code with line-number diagnostics = fix and re-pack.

## Common pitfalls

- **Legacy `.doc` (binary) is not supported.** Convert with `soffice --convert-to docx input.doc` first.
- **List numbering breaks after edits.** Numbering lives in `word/numbering.xml` keyed by `numId`. If you delete a list, also delete its numId reference; if you reorder, don't change IDs.
- **Headers and footers are separate parts** (`word/header1.xml`, etc.). Edits to body content don't touch them.
- **Pandoc reference-doc passes paragraph styles only.** Custom XML parts (comments, tracked changes baseline) are not carried over.
- **Don't pretty-print whitespace inside `<w:t>` elements.** Pretty-printing breaks runs that depend on exact spacing.
- **Tables: dual width specs.** Each cell needs both `columnWidths` (in `<w:tblGrid>`) and per-cell `<w:tcW w:type="dxa">`. Percentages (`pct`) render fine in Word but break in Google Docs.

## Out of scope

- Reading: use the `read` tool.
- Producing PDFs from .docx: pipe through `soffice --convert-to pdf` after this skill is done.
- Signing / encryption / DRM.
- Word macros (`.docm` with VBA).



## Skill: pptx

---
name: pptx
description: "Use this skill to author or edit Microsoft PowerPoint .pptx files. Covers generating decks from scratch (HTML+PptxGenJS, Marp markdown-to-slides, or python-pptx), editing existing decks in place, and validating output. For READING existing .pptx files, use the harness `read` tool — do not invoke this skill. Triggers: 'build a deck', 'create slides', 'edit slide N', 'add a chart slide'. Does NOT apply to .pdf, .docx, .xlsx, or .ppt (legacy)."
---

# PPTX authoring and editing

> **Reading is not in scope.** To read an existing .pptx, use the harness `read` tool (markitdown extracts slide text). This skill is for *writing* and *editing*.

## Quick reference

| Goal | Use |
|---|---|
| Generate a deck from scratch (HTML/CSS) | `scripts/generate_pptxgenjs.js` |
| Generate a deck from markdown | `scripts/generate_marp.sh` |
| Build slides programmatically | `python-pptx` directly |
| Edit a shape on an existing slide | `scripts/edit_shape.py` (JSON patch) |
| Add or remove a slide | unpack → edit → pack |
| QA a deck deterministically | `scripts/deterministic_qa.py` |
| Validate before delivery | `scripts/validate.py` |

## Generation modalities

**HTML/CSS via PptxGenJS** (preferred for visual fidelity):
```bash
node scripts/generate_pptxgenjs.js deck.json out.pptx
```
`deck.json` describes slides as a JSON tree; the script invokes PptxGenJS (and html2pptx for HTML inputs) to produce a fully-editable .pptx. Best for branded decks with gradients, custom fonts, complex shapes.

**Markdown via Marp**:
```bash
bash scripts/generate_marp.sh deck.md out.pptx
```
Best for content-heavy decks (lectures, reports) where markdown is more natural than JSON.

**Programmatic via python-pptx**:
Best when shapes are computed (e.g., one slide per data row). Requires manual EMU positioning.

## Editing existing decks

Three-step pattern, like docx:
```bash
python scripts/unpack.py input.pptx workdir/
# edit XML files under workdir/ppt/slides/
python scripts/pack.py workdir/ output.pptx
python scripts/validate.py output.pptx
```

For surgical shape edits without unpacking, use `edit_shape.py`:
```bash
python scripts/edit_shape.py input.pptx \
  --slide 2 --shape "Title 1" --op set_text --value "New title"
```

JSON patch ops: `set_text`, `set_position` (EMU), `set_size`, `recolor`, `delete`.

## OOXML gotchas specific to pptx

- **Use `defusedxml.minidom`, NOT `xml.etree.ElementTree`.** ElementTree corrupts presentation namespaces during round-tripping. `unpack.py` and `pack.py` use minidom; if you write your own XML manipulation, do the same.
- **EMU units everywhere.** 1 inch = 914400 EMU. Slide positions, sizes, font sizes (in pt × 100) all use derived EMU values.
- **Placeholders vs free shapes.** Placeholders inherit from slide masters; free shapes don't. Editing a placeholder's text is `<a:t>` content; editing its layout requires master-slide changes.
- **Don't pretty-print pptx XML on pack.** Whitespace-significant runs (`<a:r>`) break if reformatted. `pack.py` preserves the original whitespace.
- **Slide cloning is more than a file copy.** Use `unpack` + `pack` — manual file copies miss the rIds in `_rels/` and the `Content_Types.xml` registration.

## Deterministic QA loop

After every generation, run:

```bash
python scripts/thumbnail.py deck.pptx thumbs/   # PDF + JPEGs per slide
python scripts/deterministic_qa.py deck.pptx > qa.json
```

`deterministic_qa.py` checks:
- Shape bounding boxes don't extend past slide edges
- No two shapes overlap with > 50% area intersection
- Font sizes ≥ 11pt for body text, ≥ 18pt for titles
- All placeholders are filled (no `Click to add title` defaults)
- Bullet lists don't exceed 7 items per slide

Output is JSON listing each violation with slide number and shape id. Fix violations and re-render.

(A vision-model QA pass is intentionally out of scope for v1. Add `--use-vision` later if deterministic checks miss layout issues.)

## Validation gate

**Always run `validate.py` before declaring done.** Schema-validates against ECMA-376 PresentationML XSDs, checks rId consistency, content-type registration.

## Out of scope

- Reading: use the `read` tool.
- SmartArt creation (limited python-pptx support).
- Complex embedded charts beyond what python-pptx exposes.
- Slide transitions / animations (rarely matter for legal output).
- Vision-model layout review (deferred to v2).



## Skill: xlsx

---
name: xlsx
description: "Use this skill to author or edit Microsoft Excel .xlsx files. Covers building workbooks with formulas, editing existing files, recalculating formulas, and scanning for #REF!/#DIV/0!/#VALUE! errors. For READING existing .xlsx files, use the harness `read` tool — do not invoke this skill. Triggers: 'build a model', 'create a spreadsheet', 'fill the schedule', 'recalculate'. Does NOT apply to .pdf, .docx, .pptx, or .xls (legacy Excel)."
---

# XLSX authoring and editing

> **Reading is not in scope.** To read an existing .xlsx, use the harness `read` tool (pandas extracts every sheet as a markdown table). This skill is for *writing*, *editing*, and *recalculating*.

## Quick reference

| Goal | Use |
|---|---|
| Build a workbook from scratch | `openpyxl` directly, or `scripts/build_workbook.py` for banker conventions |
| Edit cells in an existing file | `openpyxl.load_workbook(...)` → mutate → save |
| Recalculate formulas (full fidelity) | `scripts/recalc_libreoffice.py` |
| Recalculate formulas (no LibreOffice) | `scripts/recalc_pure_python.py` |
| Scan for formula errors | `scripts/scan_errors.py` |
| Validate before delivery | `scripts/validate.py` |

## Banker conventions (mandatory for financial models)

Apply these to every workbook unless the task explicitly overrides:

- **Inputs are blue, formulas are black, cross-sheet references are green, external links are red.** Use `Font(color='0000FF')` etc.
- **Negatives in parentheses, not minus signs.** Use number format `#,##0;(#,##0)`.
- **Red negatives in P&L tables.** Use `#,##0;[Red](#,##0)`.
- **Accounting format for currency.** `_-* #,##0_-;-* #,##0_-;_-* "-"_-;_-@_-` (or the localized equivalent).
- **Multiples shown as `0.0x`**, not `0.0` followed by an "x" character. Format: `0.0"x"`.
- **Underline-only on totals**, not bold-and-underline. Use `Border(bottom=Side(style='thin'))`.
- **No merged cells in input ranges.** Merged cells break formulas that reference them; reserve merging for headers and titles only.
- **Units in adjacent cells**, not in the cell with the value. `($M)` next to the value, not `"$1,234M"` as a string.

`scripts/build_workbook.py` applies these conventions automatically given a JSON spec.

## Formula authoring

- **Always emit formulas, never calculated values.** If the user wants `revenue × growth`, write `=B2*C2`, not `1234.56`. The recalc step materializes values.
- **Use named ranges** for cross-sheet inputs. `wb.defined_names["assumptions"] = DefinedName(...)`. Easier to audit.
- **Document units in adjacent cells** so the model is self-explanatory.
- **No volatile functions in hot paths.** `OFFSET`, `INDIRECT`, `NOW`, `TODAY` recalculate on every change and slow large workbooks.

## Recalculation — choose your engine

`openpyxl` writes formula *strings*; it does not evaluate them. You must recalculate before delivery, otherwise consumers will see `=B2*C2` literal text where they expect numbers (in some readers) or stale cached values (in others).

**LibreOffice path** (`recalc_libreoffice.py`) — ground truth:
```bash
python scripts/recalc_libreoffice.py input.xlsx output.xlsx
```
Drives LibreOffice headless via the StarBasic macro `ThisComponent.calculateAll(); ThisComponent.store()`. Slow (~5–10s per workbook) but matches Excel for nearly every function. Use this when the workbook contains modern Excel features.

**Pure-Python path** (`recalc_pure_python.py`) — fast, partial:
```bash
python scripts/recalc_pure_python.py input.xlsx output.xlsx
```
Uses `xlcalculator` to evaluate every formula in pure Python. Fast (~0.5s per workbook). Covers ~80% of common functions: arithmetic, `SUM`, `IF`, `VLOOKUP`, `INDEX`/`MATCH`, basic string/date functions.

**Does NOT support**: `XLOOKUP`, `LET`, dynamic arrays (`FILTER`, `SEQUENCE`, `UNIQUE`), `LAMBDA`, `BYROW`, `TEXTJOIN` with refs, structured table references, most modern (post-2019) Excel features.

If you used any of those, run the LibreOffice path. The pure-Python path is for CI environments without LibreOffice.

## Error scan

After every recalc, scan for formula errors:

```bash
python scripts/scan_errors.py output.xlsx > errors.json
```

Reports every cell whose computed value matches `#REF!`, `#DIV/0!`, `#VALUE!`, `#NAME?`, `#NULL!`, `#NUM!`, or `#N/A`. Output is JSONL with `{sheet, address, value}` per line.

If errors exist, fix and re-recalc. Don't ship a workbook with `#REF!`s — it's the most common reason a deliverable fails QA.

## Validation gate

`scripts/validate.py output.xlsx` schema-validates against ECMA-376 SpreadsheetML XSDs and confirms ZIP integrity, content-type registration, sheet relationships.

## Out of scope

- Reading: use the `read` tool.
- **PivotTables** — `openpyxl` round-trips existing pivots but cannot create or modify them. If a task requires pivot creation, escalate (Windows-only via COM, not portable).
- **DAX measures and Power Pivot** — `openpyxl` can't write these. Same limitation.
- **VBA macros (`.xlsm`)** — out of scope for this skill. Macros require Excel runtime.
- **Conditional formatting beyond simple cell-value rules** — `openpyxl` supports basic CF; complex rules (top-N, data bars across sheets) often fail to round-trip.
- **Charts beyond the python-pptx-equivalent set** — line/bar/scatter work; combo charts and trendlines round-trip unreliably.

Father submits that this resolved matter, now more than three years old, does not warrant any restrictions on his residential time with the children or his decision-making authority.

13\. In proposing this plan, Father has considered the factors set forth in RCW 26.09.187(3)(a), including the relative strength, nature, and stability of the children\'s relationship with each parent; each parent\'s past and potential future performance of parenting functions; the emotional, physical, and developmental needs of the children; the children\'s relationship with siblings and other significant adults in their lives; the wishes of the parents; and the children\'s need for stability and continuity of relationships. Father submits that the plan set forth herein addresses each of these factors and provides a schedule and decision-making framework that will promote the children\'s overall well-being, foster the children\'s emotional and developmental growth, and preserve meaningful and substantial relationships between the children and both parents.

14\. Father believes that the equal residential schedule proposed herein, together with the joint decision-making provisions and cooperative parenting framework, represents the arrangement most likely to serve the children\'s long-term best interests and promote their healthy adjustment to the family\'s new circumstances.

**[III. RESIDENTIAL SCHEDULE]{.underline}**

**[A. Regular School-Year Residential Schedule]{.underline}**

15\. During the regular school year, the children\'s residential time shall be divided equally between the parents on a week-on, week-off alternating schedule. Each parent shall have the children for seven consecutive overnights during each two-week cycle, resulting in an equal division of residential time (fifty percent to each parent).

16\. The schedule shall operate as follows:

> \(a\) **Father\'s Residential Week.** Father\'s residential week shall begin on Sunday at 5:00 PM and shall continue through the following Sunday at 5:00 PM, for a total of seven overnights (Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, and Saturday nights).
>
> \(b\) **Mother\'s Residential Week.** Mother\'s residential week shall begin on Sunday at 5:00 PM and shall continue through the following Sunday at 5:00 PM, for a total of seven overnights (Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, and Saturday nights).

17\. All exchanges of residential time under the regular school-year schedule shall occur on Sunday at 5:00 PM. The parent whose residential week is beginning shall receive the children at the designated exchange location at 5:00 PM.

18\. The alternating weekly schedule shall commence with Father having the first residential week following entry of the final Parenting Plan by this Court. Thereafter, the parties shall alternate weekly residential time on a continuous and uninterrupted basis throughout the school year, subject only to the holiday schedule set forth in Section IV below and the summer schedule set forth in Section V below.

19\. Each parent shall be responsible for all aspects of the children\'s daily care during his or her residential week, including transportation to and from school, meals, hygiene, bedtime routines, homework supervision, and ensuring the children\'s attendance at all scheduled school activities and extracurricular commitments.

20\. The parties shall cooperate in ensuring that the children maintain a consistent routine and sense of stability throughout both residential households. Each parent shall ensure that the children have appropriate clothing, school supplies, and personal belongings available at each residence.

21\. Each parent shall have the right to attend any and all school activities, athletic events, performances, and other public events involving the children, regardless of which parent has residential time during such events.

**[B. Midweek Contact]{.underline}**

22\. During each parent\'s residential week, the non-residential parent shall have a midweek dinner visit with the children on Wednesday from 5:00 PM to 7:30 PM.

23\. The residential parent shall make the children available for the midweek visit at the designated exchange location at 5:00 PM on Wednesday. The non-residential parent shall be responsible for picking up the children at 5:00 PM and returning them to the designated exchange location at 7:30 PM. The residential parent shall ensure the children are ready for the midweek visit at the designated time.

24\. No overnight midweek contact is proposed under this plan. The midweek dinner visit is intended to ensure that the children maintain regular and frequent contact with both parents throughout the two-week residential cycle and to minimize the length of any separation between either parent and the children.

**[IV. HOLIDAY SCHEDULE]{.underline}**

**[A. General Holiday Provisions]{.underline}**

25\. The holiday schedule set forth in this section shall take precedence over the regular residential schedule established in Section III above. If a holiday period falls during one parent\'s regular residential time but is assigned to the other parent under this holiday schedule, the holiday schedule shall control, and the regular residential schedule shall resume at the conclusion of the holiday period.

26\. Holidays shall alternate between the parents on an odd-year/even-year basis as specified below. For purposes of this plan, \"odd years\" refers to years ending in an odd number (e.g., 2025, 2027, 2029), and \"even years\" refers to years ending in an even number (e.g., 2026, 2028, 2030).

27\. Unless otherwise specified below, the holiday schedule shall govern for the duration of this Parenting Plan and shall not be superseded by voluntary agreement of the parties unless such agreement is memorialized in writing and signed by both parents.

29\. In the event that a holiday period results in one parent having the children for an extended period that would otherwise displace a significant portion of the other parent\'s regular residential time, the parties shall cooperate in adjusting the regular schedule to compensate for any resulting imbalance, provided that no such adjustment shall conflict with the holiday schedule established herein.

**[V. SUMMER SCHEDULE]{.underline}**

30\. During the summer break from school, each parent shall have the children for one-half of the summer vacation period. For purposes of this plan, the summer vacation period is defined as the period beginning the day after the last day of the Lake Washington School District\'s regular academic year through the day before the first day of the new school year.

31\. The parents shall cooperate in dividing the summer period equally. Each parent shall have the children for an approximately equal number of overnights during the summer vacation period.

32\. Each parent may plan one vacation of up to fourteen consecutive days during their summer residential time. Neither parent shall schedule a vacation that extends into the other parent\'s summer residential time without the prior written consent of the other parent.

33\. In all other respects, the summer schedule shall be governed by the principles of cooperation and flexibility, with each parent making reasonable efforts to accommodate the other parent\'s schedule and the children\'s needs. The holiday schedule set forth in Section IV shall continue to apply during the summer vacation period to the extent that any holidays fall within the summer period.

**[VI. DECISION-MAKING]{.underline}**

**[A. Day-to-Day Decisions]{.underline}**

34\. Each parent shall make decisions regarding the day-to-day care and control of the children during his or her respective residential time. Day-to-day decisions include, but are not limited to, decisions regarding bedtime routines, meals and dietary choices, hygiene and grooming, daily recreational activities, minor disciplinary matters, routine scheduling, and other decisions that are necessary in the ordinary course of caring for the children on a daily basis.

35\. Neither parent shall make a day-to-day decision that significantly and irreversibly alters the child\'s circumstances or that would have a material impact on the child\'s welfare extending beyond the immediate period of that parent\'s residential time.

**[B. Major Decisions]{.underline}**

36\. The parties shall exercise joint decision-making authority with respect to the following categories of major decisions affecting the children. Joint decision-making requires that both parents discuss and agree upon major decisions before they are implemented.

> \(a\) **Education.** The parties shall jointly make all major decisions regarding the children\'s education, including but not limited to choice of school, enrollment, withdrawal, participation in special education programs, tutoring, educational testing, grade-level advancement or retention, and any other decisions that materially affect the children\'s educational experience. Neither parent shall unilaterally enroll or withdraw a child from any school or educational program without the written consent of the other parent.
>
> \(b\) **Healthcare.** The parties shall jointly make all major decisions regarding the children\'s non-emergency healthcare, including but not limited to the selection of primary care physicians, specialists, and other healthcare providers; elective medical and dental procedures; mental health treatment and counseling; therapeutic interventions; and the administration of prescription medications on an ongoing basis. In the event of a medical emergency, the parent with residential time at that moment shall have authority to consent to emergency medical treatment and shall notify the other parent as soon as reasonably practicable.
>
> \(c\) **Extracurricular Activities.** The parties shall jointly make all major decisions regarding the children\'s extracurricular activities, including but not limited to enrollment in sports teams, leagues, and athletic programs; music lessons and performance groups; camps and summer programs; scouting organizations; and any other organized activities that require a significant commitment of the children\'s time or that entail a significant financial obligation. Neither parent shall unilaterally enroll a child in an extracurricular activity that would require participation during the other parent\'s residential time without the written consent of the other parent.
>
> \(d\) **Religious Upbringing.** The parties shall jointly make all major decisions regarding the children\'s religious upbringing, including but not limited to religious education, church or temple attendance, sacraments, and participation in religious ceremonies or programs.

37\. In the event the parties are unable to agree on a major decision in any of the categories listed above, either party may petition the Court for resolution of the disputed issue. The Court shall resolve the dispute in accordance with the best interests of the children.

38\. Each parent shall make a good-faith effort to communicate with the other parent regarding major decisions in a timely manner. Each parent shall provide the other parent with relevant information necessary to make informed major decisions, including school records, medical records, report cards, and correspondence from teachers, coaches, and healthcare providers.

**[VII. DISPUTE RESOLUTION]{.underline}**

39\. In the event the parties disagree regarding any provision of this Parenting Plan, or regarding any matter concerning the children\'s welfare that is not specifically addressed in this plan, either party may file a motion with the King County Superior Court for resolution of the dispute.

40\. The parties are encouraged to resolve disputes cooperatively and in a manner that minimizes conflict and disruption to the children. However, neither party is required to engage in any specific dispute resolution process prior to seeking court intervention. Each party reserves the right to petition the Court at any time for enforcement or interpretation of this Parenting Plan.

41\. In any dispute resolution proceeding, the Court shall consider the best interests of the children as the paramount concern. The prevailing party in any enforcement action may seek an award of reasonable attorney\'s fees and costs incurred in connection with such action, in the Court\'s discretion.

**[VIII. RELOCATION]{.underline}**

**[A. Relocation Restrictions]{.underline}**

42\. Neither parent shall relocate the children\'s principal residence more than ten miles from the current residence of the other parent without the prior written consent of the other parent or an order of the Court. For purposes of this provision, the distance shall be measured as a straight-line distance from the current residential address of the non-relocating parent.

43\. This restriction shall apply regardless of whether the proposed relocation would require a change in the children\'s school enrollment. The restriction is intended to preserve the children\'s access to both parents and to maintain the viability of the residential schedule established in this plan.

44\. Any relocation that exceeds the ten-mile radius established in this section, or any relocation out of the State of Washington, shall require either the written consent of the other parent or prior approval of the Court following a noticed hearing.

**[B. Notice of Relocation]{.underline}**

45\. A parent intending to relocate the children\'s principal residence shall provide the other parent with at least thirty days\' written notice of the intended relocation. The written notice shall include the following information:

> \(a\) The intended new address or, if the specific address is not yet known, the intended city and neighborhood;
>
> \(b\) The anticipated date of the intended move;
>
> \(c\) The reasons for the proposed relocation; and
>
> \(d\) A description of how the proposed relocation will affect the residential schedule and the children\'s access to the non-relocating parent.

46\. The non-relocating parent may object to the proposed relocation by filing a motion with the King County Superior Court within fifteen days of receiving notice of the intended relocation. Upon the filing of an objection, the proposed relocation shall be stayed pending resolution of the motion by the Court.

47\. In determining whether to approve a proposed relocation, the Court shall consider the best interests of the children, the reasons for the proposed move, the impact of the move on the children\'s relationship with the non-relocating parent, and such other factors as the Court deems relevant.

**[IX. TRANSPORTATION AND EXCHANGE]{.underline}**

48\. The parties shall mutually cooperate in transporting the children for all exchanges of residential time. Each parent is expected to exercise good faith and reasonable punctuality in all exchanges.

49\. Unless otherwise agreed by the parties in writing, all exchanges of residential time shall take place at the residence of the Father, located at 1830 Dexter Avenue N, Apt 4B, Seattle, Washington 98109. The parties may mutually agree in writing to an alternative exchange location for any individual exchange, but absent such written agreement, the default exchange location shall be Father\'s residence.

50\. The receiving parent shall pick up the children at the designated exchange location at the time specified in this Parenting Plan. For purposes of all exchanges, the receiving parent is the parent whose residential time is beginning.

51\. Neither parent shall be more than fifteen minutes late for a scheduled exchange without providing advance notice to the other parent by telephone call or text message. In the event that a parent will be more than fifteen minutes late, that parent shall notify the other parent as soon as possible with an estimated time of arrival. Repeated or habitual tardiness in excess of fifteen minutes shall constitute a basis for modification of the exchange provisions.

52\. Each parent shall ensure that the children are physically and emotionally prepared for the exchange. Neither parent shall engage in conflict, confrontation, or disparaging remarks at the time and place of exchange, and both parents shall conduct all exchanges in a civil and respectful manner.

53\. Each parent shall ensure that the children\'s personal belongings, school materials, medications, and necessary items accompany the children during each exchange.

**[X. OTHER PROVISIONS]{.underline}**

**[A. Communication Between Parents]{.underline}**

54\. The parties shall communicate regarding the children\'s welfare primarily through email or text message, unless emergency circumstances require telephone communication. All communications shall be conducted in a respectful and business-like manner, focused on the children\'s needs and the logistics of the parenting schedule.

55\. Each parent shall respond to non-emergency communications from the other parent within forty-eight hours of receipt. Emergency communications shall be responded to as soon as practicable under the circumstances.

56\. Neither parent shall disparage the other parent in the presence of the children or permit any third party to do so. Neither parent shall discuss the details of the dissolution proceedings, financial disputes, or litigation strategy in the presence of the children. Each parent shall make reasonable efforts to shield the children from parental conflict and to promote a positive image of both parents.

57\. Each parent shall promptly provide the other parent with copies of all communications received from the children\'s school, healthcare providers, and extracurricular activity organizations, including but not limited to report cards, progress reports, school newsletters, medical records, and activity schedules.

**[B. General Provisions]{.underline}**

58\. Each parent shall foster a loving and positive relationship between the children and the other parent. Neither parent shall take any action that is intended to or that has the effect of undermining, interfering with, or weakening the children\'s relationship with the other parent.

59\. Each parent shall ensure the children\'s regular and timely attendance at school and shall actively support the children\'s academic progress. Each parent shall attend parent-teacher conferences, school open houses, and other school events as his or her schedule permits.

60\. Each parent shall keep the other parent reasonably informed of the children\'s health, education, and general welfare. Each parent shall promptly notify the other parent of any significant health issue, injury, illness, behavioral concern, or educational development affecting either child.

61\. Each parent shall provide the other parent with current contact information, including residential address, telephone number, and emergency contact information. Each parent shall promptly notify the other parent of any changes to this information.

62\. Neither parent shall schedule activities for the children during the other parent\'s residential time without the prior consent of the other parent. This provision applies to all activities, including but not limited to playdates, lessons, practices, performances, appointments, and social gatherings.

63\. Each parent shall maintain a safe, clean, and appropriate living environment for the children, with adequate sleeping accommodations and space for the children\'s belongings.

64\. Each parent shall ensure that any caregiver to whom the children are entrusted during that parent\'s residential time is a responsible and trustworthy adult. Each parent shall provide the other parent with the name and contact information of any regular caregiver who provides care for the children for periods exceeding four hours.

65\. Each parent shall comply with all terms and conditions of this Parenting Plan and shall cooperate with the other parent in the implementation of its provisions. The parties acknowledge that adherence to the terms of this plan is essential to the stability and well-being of the children.

**[XI. MODIFICATION]{.underline}**

66\. This Parenting Plan may be modified upon a showing by either party that there has been a material change in circumstances affecting the welfare of the children, and that the proposed modification would serve the children\'s best interests.

67\. Any petition to modify this Parenting Plan shall be filed in the King County Superior Court, Cause No. 24-3-08471-7 SEA.

68\. Pending resolution of any modification petition, the terms of this Parenting Plan shall remain in full force and effect unless the Court enters temporary orders modifying the plan during the pendency of the modification proceeding.

69\. The parties acknowledge that the children\'s needs will change as they grow and develop, and that periodic review and adjustment of the residential schedule and other provisions of this plan may be necessary and appropriate to serve the children\'s evolving needs.

**[III. Father\'s On-Call Schedule --- Key Concern]{.underline}**

Father\'s on-call obligations as an orthopedic surgeon at Puget Sound Orthopedic Associates are central to multiple issues in this case and underlie several of the proposed changes discussed in Section IV below. The following facts are drawn from on-call schedule documentation produced by Father in discovery, covering the seven-month period from June 2024 through December 2024, as well as from Client\'s personal knowledge of Father\'s work patterns during the marriage.

Father is on-call every third weekend, from Friday at 6:00 PM through Monday at 6:00 AM. When on-call, Father may be summoned to the hospital at any time during the on-call window; orthopedic surgeries during these periods typically last between three and eight hours depending on the nature of the emergency. In addition to the weekend rotation, Father is on-call for approximately eight weeknight shifts per month, each running from 6:00 PM to 6:00 AM. These weeknight on-call shifts are scattered throughout the month and do not follow a fixed pattern.

During the marriage, when Father was on a weeknight on-call shift, Mother managed all childcare --- bedtime routines, nighttime needs, and morning preparations --- without interruption, as Father would either remain at the hospital or be available to leave at a moment\'s notice. During on-call weekends, Father\'s mother, Linda Chen (age 71, residing in Bellevue, Washington), historically watched the children when Father was called away to the hospital.

Analysis of Father\'s on-call schedule data from the seven-month discovery period indicates an approximate 60% call-in rate on weekends, meaning that on roughly three out of every five on-call weekends, Father was actually summoned to the hospital, sometimes for extended periods. On weeknights, the call-in rate was approximately 35%.

Client expressed strong concern during the December 9 meeting that Father\'s proposed week-on/week-off residential schedule is entirely silent on what happens when Father is called to the hospital during his residential time. Under the current Temporary Orders, Father has fewer overnights, and even under that more limited schedule, on-call conflicts have already arisen --- on at least two occasions since the Temporary Orders were entered, Father has left the children with Linda Chen during his residential weeknight overnights without notifying Mother or offering her the opportunity to care for the children herself. This pattern forms the factual basis for both the scheduling and right-of-first-refusal provisions discussed below.

**[IV. Client\'s Specific Concerns About Father\'s Proposed Parenting Plan]{.underline}**

The following is a section-by-section review of the issues Client identified when she reviewed Father\'s proposed Parenting Plan with counsel during the December 9, 2024 meeting.

**A. Residential Schedule --- Rejection of Equal 50/50 Week-On/Week-Off**

Client firmly opposes Father\'s proposed week-on/week-off (50/50) residential schedule. Her objections are grounded in the following:

1\. **On-call conflicts.** Father\'s on-call schedule means he cannot reliably be physically present with the children during approximately one-third of his weekend residential time and numerous weeknights. The proposed plan makes absolutely no accommodation for on-call periods --- no alternate arrangements, no notification requirements, no fallback provisions. A schedule that assigns Father equal residential time while ignoring his well-documented inability to be consistently present during that time is not in the children\'s best interest.

2\. **Historical caregiving pattern.** The children have been in Mother\'s primary care since birth. Mother voluntarily reduced her work schedule to 80% for four years (2019--2023) specifically to manage childcare. The current Temporary Orders --- under which Mother has approximately nine overnights and Father has approximately five overnights per fourteen-day cycle --- reflect this historical caregiving reality. A sudden shift to equal time would represent a significant and destabilizing departure from the children\'s established routine.

3\. **GAL interim recommendation.** Guardian ad Litem Karen Lindstrom\'s interim verbal recommendation at the November 22, 2024 status conference favored a primary residential schedule with Mother during school weeks, with substantial Father time on weekends and during school breaks. Our responsive proposal should align closely with this recommendation.

4\. **Ethan\'s therapy logistics.** Ethan\'s standing Tuesday 4:00 PM speech therapy appointment at Eastside Pediatric Therapy in Hargrove requires a parent to be available mid-week in Hargrove. Father\'s apartment is 14.3 miles from both the school and the therapy office, and his workday typically does not conclude before 5:00 PM to 6:00 PM. Under a week-on/week-off arrangement, Father would be responsible for Tuesday transport during his weeks but may be unable to reliably fulfill this obligation given his work schedule and commute distance.

**Client\'s preferred residential schedule:** Substantially consistent with the current Temporary Orders. Mother retains primary residential time during school weeks. Father has a Wednesday overnight, alternating weekends from Friday after school through Sunday at 5:00 PM, and generous holiday and summer time as detailed below. Client is open to expanding Father\'s time modestly --- for example, adding a Friday overnight every weekend rather than only on alternating weekends --- provided that appropriate on-call provisions and right-of-first-refusal language are incorporated into the plan.

**B. Relocation Provision --- Improper Anchor Point and Insufficient Radius**

Father\'s proposed Parenting Plan restricts Mother from relocating more than ten (10) miles from Father\'s current residence at 1830 Dexter Avenue N, Apt 4B, Seattle, WA 98109. Client immediately identified two fundamental problems with this provision.

First, the restriction is anchored to Father\'s apartment rather than to the children\'s school, community, or the family home where the children actually reside. This means that if Father moves --- as he may well do, given that he is renting --- the geographic restriction on Mother would shift to follow his new address, effectively granting Father the unilateral power to alter the geographic constraint on Mother\'s housing options without any judicial oversight or Mother\'s consent.

Second, a ten-mile radius from Father\'s Seattle apartment would barely encompass Mother\'s current home in Hargrove (approximately 10.2 miles by road), meaning Mother could theoretically be in violation of the restriction at her current residence depending on how distance is measured. This is obviously unworkable.

**Client\'s position:** The anchor point for any relocation restriction should be Rose Hill Elementary School (8110 128th Ave NE, Hargrove, WA 98033), which centers the restriction on the children\'s established school and community. The radius should be twenty-five (25) miles. Additionally, Client noted that Father\'s plan requires only thirty (30) days\' written notice before relocation. Washington\'s child relocation statute, RCW 26.09.440, requires a minimum of sixty (60) days\' notice. Client requests ninety (90) days\' advance written notice plus prior court approval for any relocation by either parent beyond twenty-five miles from Rose Hill Elementary.

**C. Decision-Making Authority --- Education**

Father proposes joint decision-making authority on all major decisions, including education, healthcare, and extracurricular activities, with no tie-breaking mechanism and no dispute-resolution process in the event the parties cannot agree.

Client objects specifically to joint education decision-making authority without a tie-breaker, based on the following facts:

> • Father attended only one (1) of six (6) IEP meetings for Ethan conducted between 2022 and 2024.
>
> • Mother has been the sole coordinator of Ethan\'s speech-language therapy, both school-based and private, since his diagnosis in May 2022.
>
> • Joint education authority without any tie-breaking mechanism could allow Father to effectively block critical decisions through inaction, silence, or disagreement. This risk is particularly acute with respect to Ethan\'s IEP, where timely parental consent and active participation are essential to maintaining and modifying services.

**Client\'s preferred decision-making structure:**

> • **Education:** Sole decision-making authority vested in Mother. In the alternative, joint decision-making with Mother designated as the tie-breaker after a fourteen (14) day written consultation period during which Father may provide input and express his position.
>
> • **Healthcare:** Joint decision-making, with Mother designated as tie-breaker if the parties are unable to reach agreement within fourteen (14) days.
>
> • **Extracurricular activities:** Joint decision-making, with Mother designated as tie-breaker if the parties are unable to reach agreement within fourteen (14) days.

**D. Right of First Refusal --- Absent from Father\'s Plan**

Father\'s proposed Parenting Plan contains no right-of-first-refusal provision whatsoever. This is a significant omission given Father\'s on-call schedule and the well-documented frequency with which he relies on substitute childcare --- historically, his mother, Linda Chen (age 71, Bellevue, Washington) --- when he is called to the hospital during periods when he is responsible for the children.

Client\'s position is straightforward: when either parent will be absent from the children for a period exceeding four (4) consecutive hours during that parent\'s residential time, the absent parent must first offer the other parent the opportunity to care for the children before arranging third-party care. This right of first refusal should be mutual, applying equally to both Mother and Father.

Notification of the anticipated absence should be provided as far in advance as practicable. In the case of scheduled on-call shifts, Father should provide at least forty-eight (48) hours\' advance notice. For unplanned absences --- such as an emergency hospital call --- notification should be provided immediately upon learning of the absence, and in no event less than two (2) hours before the parent must leave, or immediately if the absence arises with less than two hours\' notice.

Client emphasized that this provision is not intended as a criticism of Linda Chen\'s fitness or caregiving ability. The grandmother\'s age alone is not a basis for concern, and Client acknowledged that Linda Chen has a loving relationship with the children. The principle at stake is simply that a child\'s parent should have priority over any third-party caregiver when available and willing to provide care.

**E. Ethan\'s Special Needs --- No Provisions in Father\'s Plan**

Father\'s proposed Parenting Plan contains no specific provisions whatsoever addressing Ethan\'s diagnosed speech-language delay, his active IEP at Rose Hill Elementary, his private speech-language therapy schedule, or which parent bears responsibility for coordinating these services. This omission is particularly concerning given that Ethan\'s therapy is ongoing, his progress --- while encouraging --- remains well below age-level expectations, and any disruption to the consistency of his therapeutic regimen could jeopardize the gains he has made.

Client identified this as one of her highest-priority concerns and instructed that the responsive markup include the following provisions:

1\. A dedicated section within the Parenting Plan expressly acknowledging Ethan\'s diagnosed speech-language delay and his active IEP at Rose Hill Elementary School.

2\. Designation of Mother as the primary coordinator for all IEP meetings, communications with Rose Hill Elementary\'s special education staff, and coordination with the private speech-language pathologist, Dr. Miranda Foley, at Eastside Pediatric Therapy.

3\. A requirement that both parents support and facilitate Ethan\'s therapy schedule. Specifically, the standing Tuesday 4:00 PM private SLP appointment must be maintained regardless of which parent has residential time. The residential parent on that day is responsible for transporting Ethan to and from the appointment.

4\. A requirement that both parents attend all IEP meetings. If a parent is unable to attend, that parent must provide written input to the school and to the other parent in advance of the meeting.

5\. A prohibition against either parent unilaterally changing Ethan\'s therapeutic services, providers, or frequency of sessions without the other parent\'s prior written consent or a court order.

These provisions are supported by RCW 26.09.187(3)(a), which requires the court to consider the developmental needs of the child when establishing a parenting plan. Ethan\'s documented speech-language delay and his ongoing progress under the current therapeutic regimen make this a critical component of the plan.

**F. Holiday Schedule and Therapy Continuity**

Father\'s proposed holiday schedule assigns the Thanksgiving period --- Wednesday through Sunday --- to Father in even-numbered years. Client raised a specific concern regarding this provision: Ethan\'s regular Tuesday private SLP appointment at Eastside Pediatric Therapy falls the day immediately before the proposed Wednesday start of the Thanksgiving period. Father\'s plan is entirely silent on how therapy continuity is to be maintained during holiday periods.

Client requests that the responsive markup include a general provision requiring the residential parent during any holiday period to make reasonable efforts to maintain the children\'s regular therapy and activity schedules, including transporting them to all standing appointments that fall during the holiday period. Specifically, if Ethan\'s Tuesday SLP appointment falls on a day adjacent to or within a holiday period, the parent who has residential time on that Tuesday must ensure Ethan attends the appointment.

This concern extends well beyond Thanksgiving. During spring break, winter break, and other extended holiday periods, standing therapy appointments may fall during the non-regular parent\'s residential time. The plan must contain language ensuring that holidays do not become gaps in Ethan\'s therapeutic continuity. The same principle applies to Lily\'s extracurricular commitments --- soccer practices, games, and piano lessons --- which should be maintained to the extent reasonably practicable during holiday periods.

**G. Summer Schedule --- Undefined and Vague**

Father\'s proposed Parenting Plan states that each parent shall receive \"half the summer\" but provides no specific dates, no selection mechanism, no deadline for notification of chosen weeks, and no priority system for selection. Client identified this as a virtually guaranteed source of future conflict, particularly given Lily\'s competitive soccer schedule with Eastside FC (which runs summer training camps and tournaments) and Ethan\'s need for continued speech therapy during the summer months.

**Client\'s proposed summer schedule mechanism:**

> • Each parent selects up to three (3) non-consecutive weeks of summer vacation time, for a total of six (6) weeks of designated vacation between both parents.
>
> • Selections must be submitted in writing to the other parent by March 1 of each year.
>
> • Father selects first in odd-numbered years; Mother selects first in even-numbered years.
>
> • The remaining summer time outside of the designated vacation weeks follows the regular school-year residential schedule.
>
> • The residential parent during any summer vacation week must still make reasonable efforts to maintain Ethan\'s therapy schedule, including the standing Tuesday SLP appointment at Eastside Pediatric Therapy. If a vacation week includes travel that would prevent attendance at a Tuesday appointment, the traveling parent must coordinate with Dr. Foley\'s office to reschedule the session within the same week if possible.
>
> • Neither parent may schedule vacation travel that conflicts with the other parent\'s previously selected vacation weeks without the other parent\'s prior written consent.

**H. Transportation and Exchange Locations --- Disproportionate Burden**

Father\'s proposed plan calls for \"mutual cooperation\" on transportation matters but designates Father\'s apartment at 1830 Dexter Avenue N, Apt 4B, Seattle, as the default exchange location for all residential transitions.

Client pointed out that this arrangement is neither equitable nor child-centered. Mother\'s home is approximately 1.8 miles from Rose Hill Elementary, while Father\'s apartment is approximately 14.3 miles from the school. Requiring Mother and the children to travel to Father\'s Seattle apartment for every exchange would impose a disproportionate transportation burden on Mother, add unnecessary travel time for the children, and disrupt the children\'s routines --- particularly on school mornings and evenings when the children have homework, activities, and bedtime schedules to maintain.

**Client\'s proposed exchange locations:**

> • **School days:** All exchanges shall occur at Rose Hill Elementary School via the normal drop-off and pick-up process. The parent beginning their residential time picks the children up from school at dismissal; the parent ending their residential time drops the children off at school that morning. This eliminates the need for any direct parent-to-parent exchange on school days and provides a neutral, structured transition environment.
>
> • **Non-school days (weekends, holidays, summer):** Exchanges shall occur at a neutral midpoint location. Client suggests the Hargrove Park & Ride or a similar equidistant public location to be agreed upon by the parties or, if they cannot agree, designated by the court.
>
> • **Transportation obligation:** The receiving parent picks up the children; the returning parent drops them off. This shares the driving burden equitably between the parties.

**I. Overnight Guest Restriction**

Father\'s proposed Parenting Plan contains no provision whatsoever regarding overnight guests of a romantic nature when the children are present in either parent\'s home.

Client specifically requests that the responsive markup include a mutual restriction applicable to both parents: for the first twelve (12) months following entry of the final Parenting Plan, neither parent shall have overnight guests of a romantic nature in the residence when the children are present. Client emphasized that this provision should be reciprocal and apply equally to both parents. She is not targeting Father specifically and acknowledged that she herself would be bound by the same restriction. Her concern is that the children are navigating a significant transition, and a period of stability free from the introduction of new romantic partners into the household is important for their adjustment.

**[V. Additional Provisions Client Wants Included in Markup]{.underline}**

The following items were flagged for inclusion in the responsive Parenting Plan markup. Some were identified by Client during the December 9 meeting; others arise from counsel\'s independent review of Father\'s proposed plan and are noted here for completeness.

**A. Virtual/Electronic Communication**

Father\'s proposed plan is entirely silent on telephone and video communication between the non-residential parent and the children during the other parent\'s residential time. While this gap was not specifically raised by Client during the meeting, counsel identifies it as a significant omission that should be addressed in the markup. The responsive plan should include a provision permitting each parent one phone or video call per day with the children during the other parent\'s residential time, not to exceed twenty (20) minutes, scheduled between 6:00 PM and 7:30 PM. Neither parent shall monitor, record, or interfere with such communications.

**B. Dispute Resolution Mechanism**

Father\'s proposed plan provides no dispute resolution process between disagreement and court filing. Client expressed frustration with litigation costs during the meeting and a strong preference for mediation as a first step before resorting to judicial intervention. The responsive markup should include a stepped dispute resolution process: (1) direct negotiation between parents for fourteen (14) days; (2) mediation with a mutually agreed family mediator --- Client mentioned Northgate Mediation Services, which was referenced in the Temporary Orders --- within thirty (30) days; and (3) court filing only after mediation has been attempted in good faith. This approach is consistent with the legislative preference for alternative dispute resolution expressed in RCW 26.09.015.

**C. Relocation Notice Period**

As noted in Section IV.B above, Father\'s plan requires only thirty (30) days\' notice before relocation, which falls short of the sixty (60) day minimum mandated by RCW 26.09.440. Client requests ninety (90) days\' advance written notice plus court approval for relocations beyond twenty-five (25) miles from Rose Hill Elementary. This is restated here as a standalone action item to ensure it is incorporated into the markup as a discrete provision.

**[VI. Summary of Client Priorities --- Ranked]{.underline}**

The following is a ranked summary of Mother\'s goals for the responsive Parenting Plan markup, organized by importance as expressed during the December 9, 2024 meeting:

1\. **Primary residential time during school weeks.** Maintain a schedule substantially consistent with the current Temporary Orders --- Mother approximately nine (9) overnights and Father approximately five (5) overnights per fourteen-day cycle --- to ensure stability, continuity, and particularly to protect Ethan\'s therapy schedule and school-based services.

2\. **On-call provisions and right of first refusal.** Father must provide Mother with at least forty-eight (48) hours\' advance notice of on-call periods that fall during his residential time. Mother shall have the right of first refusal when Father will be absent from the children for more than four (4) consecutive hours during his residential time, before any third-party care is arranged.

3\. **Sole decision-making authority on education, or joint with Mother as tie-breaker.** Father\'s documented lack of engagement with Ethan\'s IEP --- attendance at only one of six meetings --- makes unfettered joint education authority unworkable and potentially detrimental to Ethan\'s educational and therapeutic progress.

4\. **Ethan\'s therapy protections.** Dedicated provisions in the plan addressing IEP coordination, the Tuesday SLP appointment, designation of Mother as primary coordinator, and requirements for therapy continuity during holidays, summer, and all residential periods.

5\. **Relocation anchor point and radius.** Change the restriction from ten (10) miles from Father\'s residence to twenty-five (25) miles from Rose Hill Elementary School. Increase the notice period from thirty (30) days to ninety (90) days, with court approval required for relocations beyond the twenty-five-mile radius.

6\. **Transportation and exchange locations.** School-based exchanges on school days; neutral midpoint location on non-school days. Reject Father\'s apartment as the default exchange location.

7\. **Summer schedule specificity.** Three (3) weeks per parent, selections due by March 1 each year, alternating first-pick years, with requirements to maintain Ethan\'s therapy schedule during summer vacation periods.

8\. **Overnight guest restriction.** Mutual twelve-month restriction on overnight guests of a romantic nature when the children are present, applicable equally to both parents.

9\. **Extracurricular continuity.** Both parents required to facilitate Lily\'s competitive soccer (Eastside FC --- Tuesday and Thursday practices at 5:30--7:00 PM, Saturday games) and piano lessons (Wednesdays 4:00--4:45 PM) regardless of the residential schedule, to the extent reasonably practicable.

**[VII. Next Steps and Deadlines]{.underline}**

The following action items and deadlines were identified during and following the December 9, 2024 meeting:

> • **Responsive Parenting Plan Markup Due:** January 10, 2025 (thirty-one days from the date of this memorandum). This is the deadline for filing and service.
>
> • **Draft Markup Completion:** Sarah Whitfield to prepare a complete draft of the responsive Parenting Plan markup by December 30, 2024, for internal review within the firm.
>
> • **Client Review Call:** Schedule a follow-up telephone conference with Client for January 3, 2025, to review the draft markup in detail before finalization and filing. Client confirmed her availability on that date.
>
> • **GAL Final Report:** Guardian ad Litem Karen Lindstrom\'s final written report is anticipated in February 2025. Our responsive positions should align closely with Ms. Lindstrom\'s interim verbal recommendation where possible, to maximize the likelihood of a favorable final report.
>
> • **Trial Date:** April 14, 2025, before the Honorable Judge Patricia M. Okafor, King County Superior Court, Case No. 24-3-08471-7 SEA.
>
> • **Settlement Conference:** Consider requesting a settlement conference after the responsive markup is filed, to attempt resolution of parenting plan issues before trial. Discuss timing and strategy with Client during the January 3 call.
>
> • **On-Call Schedule Documentation:** Review and organize Father\'s on-call schedule documentation produced in discovery (covering June 2024 through December 2024) to support the proposed on-call notification and right-of-first-refusal provisions. Prepare a summary chart showing call-in frequency for use at mediation and/or trial.
>
> • **Updated Therapy Progress Report:** Contact Dr. Miranda Foley at Eastside Pediatric Therapy to obtain an updated progress report for Ethan, documenting his current speech-language status and the importance of continued consistent therapy. This report will support our proposed Ethan-specific provisions and should be obtained no later than January 31, 2025, to inform the GAL\'s final report as well.

**[VIII. Closing]{.underline}**

This memorandum is privileged and confidential attorney work product prepared in anticipation of litigation. It reflects the mental impressions, conclusions, opinions, and legal strategies of counsel. It is intended solely for internal use within Whitfield Family Law Group and should not be distributed, disclosed, or shared outside the firm under any circumstances.

WHITFIELD FAMILY LAW GROUP

Sarah Whitfield WSBA No. 31284 600 University Street, Suite 1410 Seattle, WA 98101

Date: December 10, 2024
