IN THE SUPERIOR COURT OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON IN AND FOR KING COUNTY

**No. 24-3-08471-7 SEA**

In re the Marriage of:

**JESSICA MALLORY-CHEN,**

> Petitioner,

and

**DAVID ALLEN CHEN,**

> Respondent.

**TEMPORARY ORDERS REGARDING RESIDENTIAL SCHEDULE, TEMPORARY SUPPORT, AND RESTRAINING PROVISIONS**

Filed in Open Court: September 30, 2024 Clerk of the Superior Court, King County, Washington

**[I. PRELIMINARY RECITALS AND PROCEDURAL BACKGROUND]{.underline}**

This matter came before the Court on Petitioner\'s Motion for Temporary Orders on September 27, 2024. Petitioner, Jessica Mallory-Chen (hereinafter \"Mother\" or \"Petitioner\"), appeared in person and through her attorney of record, Sarah Whitfield, WSBA No. 31284, of Whitfield Family Law Group. Respondent, David Allen Chen (hereinafter \"Father\" or \"Respondent\"), appeared in person and through his attorney of record, Gregory Holt, WSBA No. 27651, of Holt & Cromdale Consulting Family Law PLLC.

The Court has reviewed the pleadings on file herein, including but not limited to: the Petition for Dissolution of Marriage filed August 19, 2024; Petitioner\'s Motion for Temporary Orders and supporting declaration; Respondent\'s Response to Motion for Temporary Orders and supporting declaration; the financial declarations of both parties, filed pursuant to King County Local Rule 12; the declarations of Linda Chen, Dr. Miranda Foley, and Jennifer Tran submitted in support of the respective parties\' positions; and all exhibits attached thereto. The Court further heard oral argument from both counsel on September 27, 2024, and took the matter under advisement.

The Court finds the following background facts to be undisputed or established by a preponderance of the evidence for purposes of these temporary orders:

The parties were lawfully married on August 17, 2013, in King County, Washington. The parties physically separated on August 3, 2024, when Respondent vacated the family residence. Petitioner filed the Petition for Dissolution of Marriage on August 19, 2024.

There are two minor children born of the marriage: **Lily Mallory-Chen**, born June 22, 2016, age eight (8); and **Ethan Mallory-Chen**, born September 3, 2019, age five (5). Both children currently attend Rose Hill Elementary School in the Lake Washington School District, Hargrove, Washington. Ethan Mallory-Chen has been diagnosed with a speech-language delay and currently receives school-based speech-language services through an active Individualized Education Program (IEP), as well as private speech-language therapy with Dr. Miranda Foley at Eastside Pediatric Therapy, Hargrove, Washington.

Having considered the foregoing pleadings, declarations, financial documents, exhibits, and oral argument, and being fully advised in the premises, the Court enters the following temporary orders:

**[II. TEMPORARY FINDINGS OF FACT]{.underline}**

The Court makes the following findings of fact for the limited purpose of these temporary orders, pursuant to RCW 26.09.060 and RCW 26.09.191. These findings are provisional and shall not be binding at trial.

**Finding 1 --- Primary Caregiver.** The Court finds that Petitioner (Mother) has been the primary caretaker of both minor children since birth. Mother reduced her employment schedule to eighty percent (80%), working four days per week, from 2019 through 2023, in order to manage the day-to-day childcare responsibilities for both children, including school drop-off and pick-up, supervision of homework and school-related activities, coordination of medical and therapeutic appointments, and management of extracurricular activities. Mother returned to full-time employment in January 2024. Even after returning to full-time work, Mother has remained the parent primarily responsible for coordinating the children\'s medical care, school communications, IEP meetings, and extracurricular schedules. The Court finds this history relevant to the determination of the children\'s current residential needs during the pendency of this dissolution proceeding.

**Finding 2 --- Father\'s Work Schedule.** The Court finds that Respondent (Father) is employed as an orthopedic surgeon at Puget Sound Orthopedic Associates, a multi-physician surgical practice in Seattle, Washington. Father\'s regular weekday work schedule typically requires him to leave the family home by 6:15 AM and return between 7:00 PM and 8:30 PM. In addition to his regular weekday hours, Father is on-call approximately every third weekend, from Friday at 6:00 PM through Monday at 6:00 AM, and approximately eight (8) additional weeknight on-call shifts per month. The Court finds that Father\'s on-call schedule is a material consideration in determining an appropriate temporary residential schedule, as on-call obligations may require Father to leave his residence on short notice to attend to surgical emergencies, potentially for extended periods of time, during overnight and weekend hours when the children would be in his care.

**Finding 3 --- Impact of On-Call Obligations on Childcare.** The Court finds that when Father is on-call, he may be called to the hospital at any time, and surgical procedures may last between three (3) and eight (8) hours. Father\'s declaration and the declaration of Linda Chen confirm that during such periods, Father has historically relied on his mother, Linda Chen, age seventy-one (71), residing in Bellevue, Washington, to travel to the family residence to provide substitute childcare for the minor children. While the Court recognizes Grandmother Chen\'s willingness and capability to assist, the Court finds that the unpredictability and frequency of Father\'s on-call obligations require specific provisions to ensure the minor children are adequately supervised during all residential periods, and that Mother, as the children\'s other parent and a nearby resident, should be afforded the right of first refusal for childcare during Father\'s on-call absences.

**Finding 4 --- Current Residences and Proximity to School.** Mother continues to reside at the family home located at 4215 NE 72nd Street, Hargrove, Washington 98033, which is located approximately 1.8 miles from Rose Hill Elementary School, the children\'s current school. Father relocated on August 3, 2024, to a two-bedroom apartment at 1830 Dexter Avenue N, Apartment 4B, Seattle, Washington 98109, which is approximately 14.3 miles from Rose Hill Elementary School. The Court notes the substantial distance differential between the two residences relative to the children\'s school and the practical implications this has for school-day transportation, exchanges, and the children\'s morning and evening routines during the school year.

**Finding 5 --- Children\'s Special Needs, Activities, and Therapeutic Services.** Ethan Mallory-Chen has a diagnosed speech-language delay and receives school-based speech-language therapy twice weekly, on Mondays and Thursdays, through an active IEP administered by the Lake Washington School District. In addition, Ethan receives private speech-language therapy with Dr. Miranda Foley at Eastside Pediatric Therapy, located at 12020 113th Avenue NE, Suite 200, Hargrove, Washington 98034, every Tuesday at 4:00 PM. Mother has been the parent primarily responsible for coordinating Ethan\'s therapy schedule, communicating with service providers, and attending IEP meetings. Lily Mallory-Chen participates in competitive youth soccer with Eastside FC, with practices on Tuesdays and Thursdays from 5:30 PM to 7:00 PM and games on Saturday mornings, and takes piano lessons on Wednesdays from 4:00 PM to 4:45 PM. The Court finds that continuity in the children\'s therapeutic and extracurricular schedules is important to their well-being and development.

**Finding 6 --- Incomes of the Parties.** For purposes of temporary child support, the Court finds as follows: Petitioner (Mother) is employed as a Senior Marketing Manager at Cascadia Health Solutions, Inc., with an annual base salary of \$168,000 and a twenty percent (20%) annual bonus target of \$33,600, for total annual compensation of approximately \$201,600. Respondent (Father) is employed as an orthopedic surgeon at Puget Sound Orthopedic Associates, with approximate total annual income of \$485,000, inclusive of base salary, surgical bonuses, and partnership distributions, based upon Father\'s 2023 tax return and year-to-date income documentation provided to the Court.

**Finding 7 --- Family Home.** The family home located at 4215 NE 72nd Street, Hargrove, Washington 98033, was acquired during the marriage and is presumptively community property. The home has an estimated fair market value of approximately \$1,350,000, based on a comparative market analysis submitted by Petitioner, with a current mortgage balance of approximately \$612,000. The approximate equity in the family home is therefore \$738,000. The monthly mortgage payment, including principal, interest, taxes, and insurance, is approximately \$3,200.

**Finding 8 --- Best Interests Standard.** The Court finds, pursuant to RCW 26.09.187, that it is in the best interests of the minor children to maintain stability and continuity in their residential, school, and therapeutic routines during the pendency of this dissolution proceeding. The Court finds that a temporary residential schedule establishing Mother as the primary residential parent during school weeks, with substantial and meaningful residential time with Father, best serves the interests and welfare of both children at this time, taking into consideration the children\'s ages, Ethan\'s therapeutic needs, the children\'s established routines, the proximity of Mother\'s residence to the children\'s school and activities, and Father\'s demanding work and on-call schedule.

**[III. TEMPORARY RESIDENTIAL SCHEDULE]{.underline}**

Based upon the foregoing findings of fact and the applicable legal standards under RCW 26.09.187 and RCW 26.09.191, the Court orders the following temporary residential schedule:

**Section 3.1 --- School-Year Schedule (Regular Two-Week Rotation)**

The following schedule shall apply during the regular school year, defined as the period during which the Lake Washington School District is in session for regular instruction, excluding holidays and school breaks addressed separately below. The schedule shall operate on a repeating two-week cycle as follows:

**Week 1:**

> \(a\) **Sunday 5:00 PM through Wednesday after school:** The children shall reside with Mother. Mother shall pick up the children on Sunday at 5:00 PM and shall be responsible for school drop-off on Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday mornings.
>
> \(b\) **Wednesday after school through Thursday morning (school drop-off):** The children shall reside with Father. Father shall pick up the children from school on Wednesday afternoon and shall be responsible for drop-off at school on Thursday morning. This constitutes one (1) overnight with Father.
>
> \(c\) **Thursday after school through Friday 5:00 PM:** The children shall reside with Mother. Mother shall pick up the children from school on Thursday afternoon.
>
> \(d\) **Friday 5:00 PM through Sunday 5:00 PM:** The children shall reside with Father. Father shall pick up the children at 5:00 PM on Friday. This constitutes two (2) overnights with Father. This is Father\'s weekend.

**Week 2:**

> \(a\) **Sunday 5:00 PM through Wednesday after school:** The children shall reside with Mother. Mother shall pick up the children on Sunday at 5:00 PM and shall be responsible for school drop-off on Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday mornings.
>
> \(b\) **Wednesday after school through Thursday morning (school drop-off):** The children shall reside with Father. Father shall pick up the children from school on Wednesday afternoon and shall be responsible for drop-off at school on Thursday morning. This constitutes one (1) overnight with Father.
>
> \(c\) **Thursday after school through the following Sunday 5:00 PM:** The children shall reside with Mother continuously. Mother shall pick up the children from school on Thursday afternoon. This is Mother\'s weekend.

**Summary of Overnights per Fourteen-Day Cycle:** Under this schedule, the children shall have nine (9) overnights with Mother and five (5) overnights with Father in each fourteen-day rotation period, for a total of fourteen (14) overnights. This allocation reflects approximately 64% residential time with Mother and 36% residential time with Father.

**Section 3.2 --- Exchange Locations**

> \(a\) **During School Days:** All exchanges occurring on regular school days shall take place at **Rose Hill Elementary School**, located at 8110 128th Avenue NE, Hargrove, Washington 98033. The transferring parent shall drop off the children at school in the morning, and the receiving parent shall pick up the children from school in the afternoon, such that no direct parent-to-parent exchange is required on school days. The Court notes that Rose Hill Elementary is located approximately 1.8 miles from Mother\'s residence and approximately 14.3 miles from Father\'s residence. The school-based exchange minimizes transitions and disruption for the children, avoids direct exchanges between the parties that may contribute to parental conflict during this early stage of the dissolution proceeding, and utilizes a neutral location familiar and comfortable to both children.
>
> \(b\) **On Non-School Days (Weekends, Holidays, and Breaks):** The receiving parent shall pick up the children at the other parent\'s residence at the designated time, unless the parties agree in writing to an alternative exchange location. When pickup occurs at the other parent\'s residence, the receiving parent shall remain outside the residence, and the children shall be brought to the door by the transferring parent.

**Section 3.3 --- Father\'s On-Call Provisions (Temporary)**

In recognition of Father\'s on-call medical schedule as described in Finding 2 and Finding 3 above, and the need to ensure that the minor children are adequately supervised during all residential periods, the Court orders the following provisions:

> \(a\) **Advance Notice of On-Call Schedule.** Father shall provide Mother with his on-call schedule no less than seven (7) calendar days in advance of each on-call period that falls during his residential time with the children. Such notice shall be provided in writing via email or through the parties\' co-parenting communication application.
>
> \(b\) **Right of First Refusal.** If Father is called to the hospital during his residential time and the children require care for a period exceeding four (4) consecutive hours, Father shall first offer Mother the opportunity to care for the children before making alternative childcare arrangements. Father shall contact Mother by telephone or text message promptly upon being called to the hospital. Mother shall have thirty (30) minutes from the time of notification to accept or decline the opportunity to care for the children during Father\'s absence.
>
> \(c\) **Alternative Childcare.** If Mother declines, fails to respond within thirty (30) minutes, or is otherwise unavailable, Father may arrange alternative childcare with an appropriate, responsible adult caregiver. Father shall inform Mother of the identity of the alternative caregiver and the expected duration of Father\'s absence within a reasonable time.
>
> \(d\) **Log of On-Call Events.** Father shall maintain a log of all on-call events that occur during his residential time, including the date, time called, time of return, and whether Mother was offered the right of first refusal. This log shall be made available to the Guardian ad Litem upon request.

The Court includes these provisions in recognition of Respondent\'s on-call medical schedule and the need to ensure the minor children are adequately supervised during all residential periods. These provisions are not intended as a limitation on Father\'s residential time, but rather as a safeguard for the children\'s welfare.

**Section 3.4 --- Children\'s Activities and Therapy**

Both parents shall make reasonable efforts to ensure the children attend their regularly scheduled extracurricular activities and therapeutic appointments during each parent\'s residential time. Neither parent shall unilaterally discontinue or materially alter the children\'s current activities or therapy without the written consent of the other parent or court order.

Specifically, the residential parent shall:

> \(a\) Transport Ethan Mallory-Chen to his Tuesday 4:00 PM private speech-language therapy appointment at Eastside Pediatric Therapy, located at 12020 113th Avenue NE, Suite 200, Hargrove, Washington 98034, with Dr. Miranda Foley;
>
> \(b\) Transport Lily Mallory-Chen to her Eastside FC soccer practices on Tuesdays and Thursdays from 5:30 PM to 7:00 PM and to Saturday morning games as scheduled by the league; and
>
> \(c\) Transport Lily Mallory-Chen to her piano lessons on Wednesdays from 4:00 PM to 4:45 PM.

Each parent shall promptly inform the other parent of any changes, cancellations, or additions to the children\'s activity or therapy schedule.

**[IV. TEMPORARY HOLIDAY AND SCHOOL BREAK SCHEDULE]{.underline}**

**Section 4.1 --- General Provision**

The Court does not establish a comprehensive holiday schedule at this time, as the Court anticipates the parties will either reach agreement on holiday allocations through negotiation or mediation, or the matter will be addressed in the context of the final parenting plan. The regular residential schedule set forth in Section 3.1 shall apply except as specifically modified below.

**Section 4.2 --- Thanksgiving 2024**

As an interim measure, the children shall spend Thanksgiving Day 2024 (Thursday, November 28, 2024) with Father from 9:00 AM through 7:00 PM. Father shall pick up the children at Mother\'s residence at 9:00 AM and return them to Mother\'s residence at 7:00 PM. Mother shall have the children for the remainder of the Thanksgiving break, including the Wednesday before Thanksgiving and the Friday through Sunday following Thanksgiving, subject to the regular residential schedule.

**Section 4.3 --- Winter Break 2024--2025**

The 2024--2025 Winter Break shall be divided equally between the parties as follows:

> \(a\) Mother shall have the children from the last day of school (anticipated to be Friday, December 20, 2024) at the regular school dismissal time through December 25, 2024, at 12:00 PM (noon).
>
> \(b\) Father shall have the children from December 25, 2024, at 12:00 PM (noon) through January 1, 2025, at 5:00 PM.
>
> \(c\) The regular residential schedule set forth in Section 3.1 shall resume when the Lake Washington School District reconvenes for regular instruction following Winter Break.

**Section 4.4 --- Future Disputes Regarding Holidays**

If the parties are unable to agree on holiday or school break scheduling beyond the provisions set forth above, either party may bring the matter before the Court by motion on the regular family law calendar, subject to the dispute resolution provisions of Section VIII below.

**[V. TEMPORARY CHILD SUPPORT]{.underline}**

**Section 5.1 --- Amount and Payment**

Respondent (Father) shall pay temporary child support to Petitioner (Mother) in the amount of **Three Thousand Eight Hundred Fifty Dollars (\$3,850.00) per month**, payable in two equal installments of One Thousand Nine Hundred Twenty-Five Dollars (\$1,925.00) each, due on the 1st and 15th of each month. Payments shall commence on October 1, 2024, and shall continue on the 1st and 15th of each subsequent month until further order of the Court. Payment shall be made by direct deposit, electronic transfer, or other method agreed upon by the parties. In the absence of agreement, payment shall be made by check mailed or delivered to Petitioner\'s counsel, Whitfield Family Law Group, at the address set forth below.

**Section 5.2 --- Basis for Calculation**

The temporary child support amount set forth above is based upon the Washington State Child Support Schedule, RCW 26.19, and the parties\' respective incomes as found above (Mother: approximately \$201,600 total annual compensation; Father: approximately \$485,000 approximate annual income), the current temporary residential schedule, the children\'s ages and needs, and the additional therapeutic expenses associated with Ethan Mallory-Chen\'s speech-language therapy. The worksheets are attached to and incorporated by reference into these temporary orders as Exhibit A.

**Section 5.3 --- Health Insurance and Unreimbursed Medical Expenses**

Father shall continue to maintain the minor children on his employer-provided health insurance plan through Puget Sound Orthopedic Associates. Neither party shall remove the children from health insurance coverage without the written consent of the other party or court order.

All unreimbursed medical, dental, therapeutic (including but not limited to speech-language therapy), orthodontic, optical, and mental health expenses for the minor children shall be divided between the parties in proportion to their respective incomes: **seventy percent (70%) Father and thirty percent (30%) Mother** (\$485,000 ÷ \$686,600 ≈ 70.6%; \$201,600 ÷ \$686,600 ≈ 29.4%, rounded for ease of administration). The party incurring such expense shall provide documentation to the other party within thirty (30) days, and the responsible party shall reimburse their proportionate share within thirty (30) days of receipt of documentation.

**Section 5.4 --- Mortgage and Household Expenses**

Father shall continue to pay the monthly mortgage on the family home at 4215 NE 72nd Street, Hargrove, Washington 98033, in the approximate amount of \$3,200 per month, as a temporary contribution to household expenses and in lieu of a separate temporary spousal maintenance award, pending resolution of property and maintenance issues. This payment is in addition to the temporary child support ordered above. This characterization is without prejudice to either party\'s position at trial as to the nature and treatment of such payments.

**[VI. TEMPORARY RESTRAINING PROVISIONS]{.underline}**

**Section 6.1 --- Mutual Restraining Order**

Both parties are hereby mutually restrained and enjoined from:

> \(a\) Molesting or disturbing the peace of the other party or the minor children, including but not limited to acts of domestic violence as defined in RCW 26.50.010, harassment, intimidation, or threats;
>
> \(b\) Destroying, concealing, encumbering, transferring, or otherwise disposing of any property in which the other party has or may have an interest, except in the usual course of business, for the necessities of life, or for reasonable attorney\'s fees in connection with this dissolution proceeding;
>
> \(c\) Making any extraordinary expenditure without the prior written consent of the other party or an order of this Court. For purposes of this provision, an \"extraordinary expenditure\" is defined as any single purchase, expenditure, or financial commitment exceeding Five Hundred Dollars (\$500.00) that is outside the scope of the party\'s ordinary and customary living expenses;
>
> \(d\) Relocating the minor children\'s principal residence more than twenty-five (25) miles from Rose Hill Elementary School, Lake Washington School District, Hargrove, Washington, without the prior written consent of the other party or prior court approval. In any event, any intended relocation of the children shall be subject to the notice requirements of RCW 26.09.440, requiring at least sixty (60) days\' advance written notice to the other party.

**Section 6.2 --- Property Preservation**

Both parties shall maintain the status quo with respect to all community and separate assets and liabilities, including but not limited to the family home, retirement accounts, 401(k) plans, investment accounts, bank accounts, and vehicles. Neither party shall close, transfer, or materially alter any financial account without the written consent of the other party or court order, except for withdrawals in the ordinary course of living expenses consistent with the party\'s historical spending patterns.

**Section 6.3 --- Insurance Preservation**

Neither party shall cancel, modify, surrender, allow to lapse, borrow against, or change the beneficiary of any existing insurance policy (including health, dental, auto, life, disability, and homeowner\'s insurance) covering the other party, the minor children, or community property without the prior written consent of the other party or an order of this Court.

**Section 6.4 --- Access to Children\'s Records**

Both parents shall have full and equal access to the minor children\'s medical, dental, therapeutic, educational, and school records. Each parent shall be entitled to communicate directly with the children\'s healthcare providers, therapists, teachers, and school administrators. Each parent shall promptly share with the other parent all material information regarding the children\'s health, education, therapy, and general welfare, including but not limited to school reports, IEP documents, progress notes, and medical records, within a reasonable time of receipt.

**[VII. GUARDIAN AD LITEM APPOINTMENT]{.underline}**

**Section 7.1 --- Appointment**

The Court determines that the appointment of a Guardian ad Litem is appropriate in this matter to investigate and report on the best interests of the minor children for purposes of the final parenting plan, in light of the parties\' inability to reach agreement on a permanent residential schedule. The Court shall appoint a Guardian ad Litem from the King County Superior Court GAL Registry.

**Section 7.2 --- Separate Appointment Order**

The order appointing the Guardian ad Litem, specifying the scope of the GAL\'s investigation and authority, shall be entered separately from these temporary orders.

**Section 7.3 --- Allocation of GAL Fees**

Fees and costs of the Guardian ad Litem shall be divided between the parties as follows: **sixty percent (60%) Father and forty percent (40%) Mother**, proportionate to the parties\' respective incomes, unless otherwise ordered by the Court. Each party shall pay their respective share directly to the GAL upon receipt of invoice.

**Section 7.4 --- Cooperation with the GAL**

Both parents shall cooperate fully with the Guardian ad Litem, including but not limited to: providing the GAL with access to the minor children at reasonable times; providing the GAL with access to the parents\' respective residences for home visits; executing any necessary authorizations for release of medical, therapeutic, educational, and other relevant records; and making themselves available for interviews and follow-up inquiries. Failure to cooperate with the GAL may result in sanctions or an adverse inference at trial.

**[VIII. TEMPORARY DISPUTE RESOLUTION]{.underline}**

**Section 8.1 --- Mediation Requirement**

If the parties are unable to resolve any dispute regarding the interpretation or implementation of these temporary orders through direct communication, they shall first attempt to resolve the matter through mediation with Northgate Mediation Services, or another mediator mutually agreed upon by the parties. Each party shall bear their own costs of mediation unless they otherwise agree in writing or the Court orders otherwise.

**Section 8.2 --- Exceptions to Mediation Requirement**

If mediation is unsuccessful after a good-faith attempt, or if mediation is impracticable under the circumstances---including but not limited to situations involving immediate safety concerns for the children, allegations of domestic violence, or time-sensitive matters that cannot reasonably await the scheduling of a mediation session---either party may bring the matter before the Court by motion on the regular family law calendar.

**Section 8.3 --- Certification of Mediation Attempt**

Neither party shall file a motion to modify these temporary orders, or a motion for contempt arising from an alleged violation of these temporary orders, without first certifying to the Court in writing that (a) the party has made a good-faith attempt at mediation, or (b) an exception under Section 8.2 applies and the basis for the exception is stated in the certification.

**[IX. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS]{.underline}**

**Section 9.1 --- Communication Between Parents**

The parties shall communicate primarily in writing---via email or a mutually agreed co-parenting application such as OurFamilyWizard or TalkingParents---regarding scheduling, the children\'s needs, and other parenting matters. Both parties shall maintain a civil, respectful, and business-like tone in all communications. Neither party shall make disparaging remarks about the other party in the presence of the minor children or in communications that are accessible to the children.

**Section 9.2 --- Telephone and Video Contact**

The non-residential parent shall have reasonable telephone or video contact with the children during the other parent\'s residential time. Such contact shall occur at reasonable times, generally between 6:00 PM and 7:30 PM unless otherwise agreed, and shall not disrupt the children\'s dinner, homework, bedtime routines, or scheduled activities. Each parent shall facilitate and encourage the children\'s contact with the other parent and shall ensure that a functioning telephone or device is available to the children for such contact.

**Section 9.3 --- Trial Date**

Trial in this matter is currently set for **April 14, 2025**. The parties shall comply with all deadlines set forth in the Case Scheduling Order entered by this Court. Failure to comply with scheduling order deadlines may result in sanctions, including but not limited to exclusion of evidence or witnesses.

**Section 9.4 --- Duration of Temporary Orders**

These temporary orders shall remain in full force and effect until modified by subsequent order of this Court, or until superseded by the entry of final orders, a final parenting plan, or a decree of dissolution in this matter.

**ORDER**

Based upon the foregoing findings and conclusions, and for good cause shown, the Court hereby ORDERS, ADJUDGES, and DECREES that the temporary orders set forth above in Sections II through IX shall be and hereby are in full force and effect as of the date of entry of this order.

**IT IS SO ORDERED this 30th day of September, 2024.**

**[Section 2: Current IEP Summary (Dated September 12, 2024)]{.underline}**

Father did not attend the meeting and did not request rescheduling or participate by telephone or other remote means. The next annual IEP review is scheduled for September 2025.

**2.2 Present Levels of Performance**

**Expressive Language:** Standardized testing using the Clinical Evaluation of Language Fundamentals --- Preschool, Third Edition (CELF-P3) places Ethan at the **31st percentile** in expressive language as of the September 2024 evaluation. At his initial evaluation in May 2022, Ethan scored at the **8th percentile** in expressive language, representing significant improvement over approximately two years of consistent intervention.

**Receptive Language:** Ethan\'s receptive language skills fall within normal limits at the 48th percentile. Receptive language is not a current area of clinical concern.

**Articulation:** Mild phonological process errors are present, consistent with age expectations, and are expected to resolve with continued intervention.

**Pragmatic/Social Communication:** Age-appropriate; no concerns noted by the IEP team.

**Academic Impact:** Ethan\'s speech-language delay affects his ability to participate fully in classroom discussions, narrate personal experiences, and express complex ideas verbally. His classroom teacher, Ms. Park, reports that Ethan sometimes becomes frustrated when unable to communicate effectively with peers, particularly during unstructured activities. Ethan continues to qualify for special education services under the Communication Disorder category. His progress has been meaningful and is directly attributable to consistent, ongoing speech-language intervention both at school and through private therapy. The IEP team recommends continued services.

**2.3 Annual Goals**

The September 2024 IEP establishes the following annual goals:

**Goal 1 --- Expressive Language:** By September 2025, Ethan will use age-appropriate grammatical structures, including complex sentences with conjunctions and correct verb tense, in 4 out of 5 opportunities during structured and unstructured classroom activities, as measured by SLP data collection and teacher observation.

**Goal 2 --- Narrative Skills:** By September 2025, Ethan will independently produce a coherent personal narrative containing at least 5 sequential events with appropriate temporal markers (e.g., \"first,\" \"then,\" \"after that\") in 3 out of 5 opportunities, as measured by SLP assessment.

**Goal 3 --- Vocabulary/Word Retrieval:** By September 2025, Ethan will demonstrate improved word retrieval by accurately naming pictured items and describing their function within 5 seconds in 80% of trials, as measured by SLP data collection.

**2.4 Services and Schedule (School-Based)**

> • **Service Type:** Speech-Language Therapy (individual and small group)
>
> • **Frequency:** Twice weekly --- **Mondays and Thursdays** during school hours
>
> • **Duration:** 30 minutes per session
>
> • **Location:** Rose Hill Elementary School, Speech-Language Services Room
>
> • **Provider:** Rachel Dominguez, M.S., CCC-SLP
>
> • **Delivery Model:** Pull-out individual session (Mondays); small group session with 1--2 peers (Thursdays)
>
> • **Consultation:** School SLP consults with classroom teacher monthly and provides home practice materials to parent(s) quarterly

The IEP specifies that home practice activities should be implemented consistently by both parents and caregivers to reinforce skills addressed in therapy sessions. To date, Mother has been the parent implementing home practice activities.

**2.5 Accommodations and Modifications**

The current IEP includes the following classroom accommodations: extended time for oral responses; preferential seating near the teacher during group instruction; visual supports and graphic organizers for language-based tasks; and teacher checks for understanding using simple yes/no or short-answer questions before expecting extended verbal responses.

**[Section 3: Private Speech-Language Therapy Records]{.underline}**

**3.1 Provider Information**

**Provider:** Dr. Miranda Foley, Ph.D., CCC-SLP **Practice:** Eastside Pediatric Therapy **Address:** 12020 113th Ave NE, Suite 200, Hargrove, WA 98034

Ethan has received private speech-language therapy from Dr. Foley since June 2022, following his May 2022 diagnosis. He was referred by his pediatrician, Dr. Priya Ramachandran at Hargrove Pediatric Associates. Ethan\'s current standing appointment is **every Tuesday at 4:00 PM** for 45-minute sessions. Mother (Jessica Mallory-Chen) has transported Ethan to and attended all private SLP sessions. Father (David Allen Chen) has not attended any private SLP sessions. Mother manages all scheduling and insurance billing for these services.

**3.2 Progress Notes Summary (Selected Dates)**

The following progress notes from Dr. Foley\'s clinical records document Ethan\'s trajectory over approximately two and a half years of treatment:

**June 14, 2022 --- Initial Evaluation:** Ethan, age 2 years 9 months, presents with significant expressive language delay. Standardized testing places expressive language at the 8th percentile. Receptive language within normal limits. Recommendations included weekly individual SLP therapy, a home practice program, and coordination with school-based services upon enrollment.

**January 10, 2023 --- 6-Month Progress Note:** Ethan demonstrating gains in mean length of utterance (MLU). Expressive language estimated at approximately the 15th percentile. Mother reports consistent home practice implementation. Continued weekly sessions recommended.

**September 5, 2023 --- 15-Month Progress Note:** Expressive language at approximately the 22nd percentile. Ethan using 3--4 word sentences consistently and beginning to use past tense verbs. Narrative skills emerging. Mother remains actively engaged in the therapy program. Father has not attended sessions. Continued weekly sessions recommended.

**March 19, 2024 --- 22-Month Progress Note:** Expressive language at approximately the 27th percentile. Ethan producing more complex sentences but still struggling with word retrieval under time pressure. Strong gains in vocabulary. Continued weekly sessions recommended to consolidate gains and target narrative skills and higher-level grammatical structures.

**November 12, 2024 --- Most Recent Progress Note:** Expressive language at the 31st percentile per most recent standardized assessment, representing significant progress from the 8th percentile baseline. Ethan now produces age-appropriate sentence structures in structured settings but continues to need support in unstructured conversational contexts. IEP goals and private therapy goals remain well-aligned. Dr. Foley\'s clinical opinion, stated in her progress note:

> *\"Ethan has made meaningful and measurable progress over the past two and a half years. This progress is directly attributable to the consistency and frequency of his therapy schedule --- both school-based (Mondays and Thursdays) and private (Tuesdays). I strongly recommend that Ethan\'s therapy schedule be maintained without interruption. Gaps in service, even of one to two weeks, can result in regression of emerging skills at this stage of development. Both parents should be actively involved in supporting therapy goals, including home practice activities.\"*

**3.3 Therapy Recommendations Going Forward**

Dr. Foley recommends continued private SLP sessions at least weekly (current Tuesday 4:00 PM schedule) for a minimum of 12 additional months, through at least November 2025, with reassessment at that time. Home practice of 15--20 minutes daily of structured language activities should be implemented by whichever parent has residential time. Dr. Foley further recommends that one parent serve as the primary coordinator between school-based and private therapy services to ensure goal alignment and avoid duplication of effort. To date, Mother has served exclusively in this coordination role. Dr. Foley is available for parent conferences and will provide reports as needed for court proceedings.

**[Section 5: Summary and Implications for Parenting Plan]{.underline}**

Ethan Mallory-Chen has a clinically significant speech-language delay that requires ongoing, consistent intervention through both school-based services (Mondays and Thursdays at Rose Hill Elementary) and private speech-language therapy (Tuesdays at 4:00 PM with Dr. Miranda Foley at Eastside Pediatric Therapy, 12020 113th Ave NE, Suite 200, Hargrove, WA 98034). Ethan has made substantial progress, improving from the 8th percentile to the 31st percentile in expressive language over approximately two years of consistent therapy. However, his treating clinician recommends at least 12 additional months of weekly therapy and has warned that gaps in service, even of one to two weeks, can result in regression of emerging skills.

Mother has been the sole parent managing Ethan\'s therapeutic and educational program. She has attended all 6 IEP meetings, transported Ethan to every private SLP appointment since June 2022, implemented daily home practice activities, and served as the sole coordinator between school-based and private therapy services. Father attended 1 of 6 IEP meetings --- the initial meeting in October 2022 --- and has not attended any private SLP sessions.

Based on the clinical and educational records summarized herein, any parenting plan entered in this matter should: (a) explicitly acknowledge Ethan\'s speech-language delay and ongoing treatment needs; (b) designate a parent responsible for IEP coordination and therapy management; (c) ensure the residential schedule does not disrupt Ethan\'s school-based therapy on Mondays and Thursdays or his private therapy on Tuesdays at 4:00 PM; (d) require the residential parent during holiday and vacation periods to make reasonable efforts to maintain Ethan\'s regular therapy schedule, including transporting him to his standing Tuesday appointment; and (e) require both parents to implement home practice activities during their respective residential time. Under RCW 26.09.187(3)(a), the court is required to consider the developmental needs of the children in establishing the parenting plan.

"""Generate a tracked-changes redline from two .docx files.

Usage:
    python redline.py original.docx revised.docx redlined.docx \
        --author "Reviewer" --date 2026-04-30

Default mode: tries the `redlines` package (PyPI, JSv4) for paragraph-level
diffs, falls back to a manual SequenceMatcher + diff-match-patch
implementation when redlines isn't available.

Output is a .docx with native <w:ins>/<w:del> revision elements that render
in Word's Track Changes pane.
"""
import argparse
import sys
import tempfile
import zipfile
from datetime import date
from difflib import SequenceMatcher
from pathlib import Path

import docx
from lxml import etree


W = "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/wordprocessingml/2006/main"
NSMAP = {"w": W}


def _paragraph_texts(path: Path) -> list[str]:
    d = docx.Document(str(path))
    return [p.text for p in d.paragraphs]


def _diff_words(a: str, b: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    """Return word-level diff ops as (op, text) pairs. op ∈ {'eq', 'ins', 'del'}."""
    try:
        from diff_match_patch import diff_match_patch
        dmp = diff_match_patch()
        diffs = dmp.diff_main(a, b)
        dmp.diff_cleanupSemantic(diffs)
        out = []
        for op, text in diffs:
            if op == 0:
                out.append(("eq", text))
            elif op == 1:
                out.append(("ins", text))
            else:
                out.append(("del", text))
        return out
    except ImportError:
        # Fallback: SequenceMatcher on words
        aw, bw = a.split(" "), b.split(" ")
        sm = SequenceMatcher(None, aw, bw)
        ops = []
        for tag, i1, i2, j1, j2 in sm.get_opcodes():
            if tag == "equal":
                ops.append(("eq", " ".join(aw[i1:i2]) + " "))
            elif tag == "delete":
                ops.append(("del", " ".join(aw[i1:i2]) + " "))

"""Add Word comments to a .docx by anchor-text matching.

Usage: python comments_add.py input.docx comments.json output.docx

comments.json is a list of objects:
    [{"anchor_text": "...", "author": "...", "comment": "..."}]

The first occurrence of each anchor is wrapped with a comment range. Pass the
same anchor multiple times to comment subsequent occurrences. Existing
comments in the document are preserved and new ones get fresh IDs.
"""
import json
import sys
import tempfile
import zipfile
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path

from lxml import etree


W = "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/wordprocessingml/2006/main"
PR = "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/package/2006/relationships"
REL = "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/officeDocument/2006/relationships"
CT = "http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/package/2006/content-types"
COMMENTS_TYPE = "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.comments+xml"
COMMENTS_REL = f"{REL}/comments"
NS = {"w": W, "pr": PR, "ct": CT}


def _next_id(comments_root) -> int:
    if comments_root is None:
        return 1
    ids = [int(c.get(f"{{{W}}}id", "0")) for c in comments_root.findall(f"{{{W}}}comment")]
    return (max(ids) + 1) if ids else 1


def _next_rid(rels_root) -> str:
    used = {r.get("Id") for r in rels_root}
    n = 1
    while f"rId{n}" in used:
        n += 1
    return f"rId{n}"


def _ensure_comments_part(wd: Path) -> Path:
    comments_path = wd / "word" / "comments.xml"
    if not comments_path.exists():
        comments_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        root = etree.Element(f"{{{W}}}comments", nsmap={"w": W})

def _make_run(text: str) -> etree.Element:
    r = etree.Element(f"{{{W}}}r")
    t = etree.SubElement(r, f"{{{W}}}t")
    t.set("{http://www.w3.org/XML/1998/namespace}space", "preserve")
    t.text = text
    return r


def _make_ins(text: str, rev_id: int, author: str, when: str) -> etree.Element:
    ins = etree.Element(f"{{{W}}}ins")
    ins.set(f"{{{W}}}id", str(rev_id))
    ins.set(f"{{{W}}}author", author)
    ins.set(f"{{{W}}}date", when)
    ins.append(_make_run(text))
    return ins


def _make_del(text: str, rev_id: int, author: str, when: str) -> etree.Element:
    d = etree.Element(f"{{{W}}}del")
    d.set(f"{{{W}}}id", str(rev_id))
    d.set(f"{{{W}}}author", author)
    d.set(f"{{{W}}}date", when)
    r = etree.SubElement(d, f"{{{W}}}r")
    t = etree.SubElement(r, f"{{{W}}}delText")
    t.set("{http://www.w3.org/XML/1998/namespace}space", "preserve")
    t.text = text
    return r.getparent()


def redline(original: Path, revised: Path, output: Path, author: str, when: str):
    # Use the original as the base document so styles/headers/footers are preserved.
    # Replace its body paragraphs with revision-marked versions.
    orig_paras = _paragraph_texts(original)
    rev_paras = _paragraph_texts(revised)

    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as workdir:
        wd = Path(workdir)
        with zipfile.ZipFile(original) as z:
            z.extractall(wd)
        doc_xml = wd / "word" / "document.xml"
        tree = etree.parse(str(doc_xml))
        root = tree.getroot()
        body = root.find(f"{{{W}}}body")
        if body is None:
            print("ERROR: no body in document.xml", file=sys.stderr)
            sys.exit(1)

        # Find sectPr to preserve at end
        sect_pr = body.find(f"{{{W}}}sectPr")
        # Remove all existing paragraphs (we rebuild)
        for p in list(body):
            if p.tag != f"{{{W}}}sectPr":
                body.remove(p)

        sm = SequenceMatcher(None, orig_paras, rev_paras)
        rev_id = 1
        for tag, i1, i2, j1, j2 in sm.get_opcodes():
            if tag == "equal":
                for text in orig_paras[i1:i2]:
                    p = etree.SubElement(body, f"{{{W}}}p")
                    if text:
                        p.append(_make_run(text))
            elif tag == "delete":
                for text in orig_paras[i1:i2]:
                    p = etree.SubElement(body, f"{{{W}}}p")
                    if text:
                        p.append(_make_del(text, rev_id, author, when))
                        rev_id += 1
            elif tag == "insert":
                for text in rev_paras[j1:j2]:
                    p = etree.SubElement(body, f"{{{W}}}p")
                    if text:
                        p.append(_make_ins(text, rev_id, author, when))
                        rev_id += 1
            elif tag == "replace":
                # Word-level diff for replaced paragraphs (assume 1:1 for now)
                pairs = list(zip(orig_paras[i1:i2], rev_paras[j1:j2]))
                # Handle unequal lengths by padding
                if len(orig_paras[i1:i2]) > len(rev_paras[j1:j2]):
                    # Extra deletions
                    pairs += [(t, "") for t in orig_paras[i1 + len(pairs):i2]]
                elif len(rev_paras[j1:j2]) > len(orig_paras[i1:i2]):
                    pairs += [("", t) for t in rev_paras[j1 + len(pairs):j2]]
                for a, b in pairs:
                    p = etree.SubElement(body, f"{{{W}}}p")
                    for op, txt in _diff_words(a, b):
                        if not txt:
                            continue
                        if op == "eq":
                            p.append(_make_run(txt))
                        elif op == "ins":
                            p.append(_make_ins(txt, rev_id, author, when))
                            rev_id += 1
                        elif op == "del":
                            p.append(_make_del(txt, rev_id, author, when))
                            rev_id += 1

        # Restore sectPr at end
        if sect_pr is not None:
            body.remove(sect_pr)
            body.append(sect_pr)

        tree.write(str(doc_xml), xml_declaration=True, encoding="UTF-8", standalone=True)

        output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        with zipfile.ZipFile(output, "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as zout:
            for p in sorted(wd.rglob("*")):
                if p.is_file():
                    zout.write(p, p.relative_to(wd).as_posix())

    print(f"OK: wrote {output}")

def _ensure_content_type(wd: Path):

    root = tree.getroot()
    has_override = any(
        o.get("PartName") == "/word/comments.xml"
        for o in root.findall(f"{{{CT}}}Override")

    """Return the first <w:r> whose <w:t> contains anchor_text and isn't used yet."""
    for r in doc_root.iter(f"{{{W}}}r"):
        if id(r) in used_runs:
            continue
        text_parts = [t.text or "" for t in r.findall(f"{{{W}}}t")]
        full_text = "".join(text_parts)
        if anchor_text in full_text:
            return r
    return None


def _wrap_run_with_comment(run, comment_id: int):
    """Insert <w:commentRangeStart>, <w:commentRangeEnd>, and reference run around run."""
    parent = run.getparent()
    if parent is None:
        return
    idx = list(parent).index(run)

    cstart = etree.Element(f"{{{W}}}commentRangeStart")
    cstart.set(f"{{{W}}}id", str(comment_id))
    cend = etree.Element(f"{{{W}}}commentRangeEnd")
    cend.set(f"{{{W}}}id", str(comment_id))

    # Reference run with commentReference
    ref_run = etree.Element(f"{{{W}}}r")
    rpr = etree.SubElement(ref_run, f"{{{W}}}rPr")
    rstyle = etree.SubElement(rpr, f"{{{W}}}rStyle")
    rstyle.set(f"{{{W}}}val", "CommentReference")
    cref = etree.SubElement(ref_run, f"{{{W}}}commentReference")
    cref.set(f"{{{W}}}id", str(comment_id))

    parent.insert(idx, cstart)
    parent.insert(idx + 2, cend)
    parent.insert(idx + 3, ref_run)


def _append_comment(comments_path: Path, comment_id: int, author: str, text: str):
    tree = etree.parse(str(comments_path))
    root = tree.getroot()
    comment = etree.SubElement(root, f"{{{W}}}comment")
    comment.set(f"{{{W}}}id", str(comment_id))
    comment.set(f"{{{W}}}author", author)
    comment.set(f"{{{W}}}date", datetime.utcnow().strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"))
    p = etree.SubElement(comment, f"{{{W}}}p")
    r = etree.SubElement(p, f"{{{W}}}r")
    t = etree.SubElement(r, f"{{{W}}}t")
    t.text = text
    tree.write(str(comments_path), xml_declaration=True, encoding="UTF-8", standalone=True)


def add_comments(input_path: Path, comments_json: Path, output_path: Path):
    items = json.loads(comments_json.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as workdir:
        wd = Path(workdir)
        with zipfile.ZipFile(input_path) as z:
            z.extractall(wd)

        comments_path = _ensure_comments_part(wd)
        _ensure_content_type(wd)
        _ensure_rel(wd)

        comments_tree = etree.parse(str(comments_path))
        next_id = _next_id(comments_tree.getroot())

        doc_path = wd / "word" / "document.xml"
        doc_tree = etree.parse(str(doc_path))
        doc_root = doc_tree.getroot()
        used_runs = set()

        for item in items:
            anchor = item["anchor_text"]
            author = item.get("author", "Reviewer")
            text = item["comment"]
            run = _find_run_with_text(doc_root, anchor, used_runs)
            if run is None:
                print(f"WARN: anchor not found: {anchor!r}", file=sys.stderr)
                continue
            used_runs.add(id(run))
            _wrap_run_with_comment(run, next_id)
            _append_comment(comments_path, next_id, author, text)
            next_id += 1

        doc_tree.write(str(doc_path), xml_declaration=True, encoding="UTF-8", standalone=True)

        output_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        with zipfile.ZipFile(output_path, "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as zout:
            for p in sorted(wd.rglob("*")):
                if p.is_file():
                    zout.write(p, p.relative_to(wd).as_posix())

    print(f"OK: wrote {output_path}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if len(sys.argv) != 4:
        print("Usage: comments_add.py <input.docx> <comments.json> <output.docx>", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(2)
    add_comments(Path(sys.argv[1]), Path(sys.argv[2]), Path(sys.argv[3]))

"""Pack a working directory back into a .docx (or any OOXML zip).

Usage: python pack.py workdir/ output.docx

Reverses smart-quote substitutions, condenses pretty-printed whitespace where
needed, and zips with [Content_Types].xml as the first entry.
"""
import sys
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path


SMART_QUOTE_REVERSE = {
    '__SQ_LDQ__': '“',
    '__SQ_RDQ__': '”',
    '__SQ_LSQ__': '‘',
    '__SQ_RSQ__': '’',
    '__SQ_NDASH__': '–',
    '__SQ_MDASH__': '—',
    '__SQ_HELLIP__': '…',
}

CONTENT_TYPES = "[Content_Types].xml"


def pack(in_dir: Path, output_path: Path):
    # Reverse smart-quote substitutions in place
    for xml_path in in_dir.rglob("*.xml"):
        try:
            text = xml_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        except (UnicodeDecodeError, OSError):
            continue
        for sub, q in SMART_QUOTE_REVERSE.items():
            text = text.replace(sub, q)
        xml_path.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")

    # Collect files; [Content_Types].xml must be first in the zip stream
    files = sorted(p for p in in_dir.rglob("*") if p.is_file())
    files.sort(key=lambda p: 0 if p.name == CONTENT_TYPES else 1)

    output_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with zipfile.ZipFile(output_path, "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as zout:
        for p in files:
            arcname = p.relative_to(in_dir).as_posix()
            zout.write(p, arcname)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if len(sys.argv) != 3:
        print("Usage: pack.py <workdir/> <output.docx>", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(2)
    pack(Path(sys.argv[1]), Path(sys.argv[2]))
=====UNPACK=====
"""Unpack a .docx (or any OOXML zip) into a working directory.

Usage: python unpack.py input.docx workdir/

Extracts the ZIP, pretty-prints each XML part for human-editability,
substitutes smart quotes with placeholder tokens so they survive editing.
"""
import sys
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path
from lxml import etree


SMART_QUOTE_SUBS = {
    '“': '__SQ_LDQ__',  # left double
    '”': '__SQ_RDQ__',  # right double
    '‘': '__SQ_LSQ__',  # left single
    '’': '__SQ_RSQ__',  # right single (also apostrophe)
    '–': '__SQ_NDASH__',
    '—': '__SQ_MDASH__',
    '…': '__SQ_HELLIP__',
}


def unpack(input_path: Path, out_dir: Path):
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with zipfile.ZipFile(input_path) as z:
        z.extractall(out_dir)

    # Pretty-print XML parts and substitute smart quotes for safe editing.
    # Skip parts where pretty-printing would break whitespace-significant runs
    # (we keep document.xml itself raw so <w:t xml:space="preserve"> stays intact).
    skip_pretty = {"document.xml", "comments.xml"}

    for xml_path in out_dir.rglob("*.xml"):
        try:
            text = xml_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        except (UnicodeDecodeError, OSError):
            continue

        # Substitute smart quotes for editing safety
        for q, sub in SMART_QUOTE_SUBS.items():
            text = text.replace(q, sub)

        if xml_path.name in skip_pretty:
            xml_path.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
            continue

        try:
            tree = etree.fromstring(text.encode("utf-8"))
            pretty = etree.tostring(
                tree, pretty_print=True, xml_declaration=True, encoding="UTF-8",
            )
            xml_path.write_bytes(pretty)
        except etree.XMLSyntaxError:
            # Leave malformed parts alone — pack.py will pass them through
            xml_path.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if len(sys.argv) != 3:
        print("Usage: unpack.py <input.docx> <workdir/>", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(2)
    unpack(Path(sys.argv[1]), Path(sys.argv[2]))

function.description: Execute a bash command and return its output. Use for running scripts, installing packages, file manipulation, and any shell operation. The working directory persists between calls.
function.name: bash

function.description: Read a file from the input directory or workspace. Handles .docx, .xlsx, .pptx, .pdf, and plain text — extraction is automatic; use this rather than a skill just to read. Use offset and limit for large files.
function.name: read

file_path.description: Relative path (resolved against workspace then input directory) or absolute path

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Optional.

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (0-based). Optional.

function.description: Write a plain markdown file (typically `response.md`) to the output directory. For binary deliverables (.docx, .xlsx, .pptx), use the file-type skill manuals — do not write raw markdown to a binary extension. Creates parent directories if needed.
function.name: write

file_path.description: Relative path under the output directory (e.g., 'response.md')

function.description: Perform exact string replacement in a file you have already created or read. The old_string must appear exactly once unless replace_all is true. Use for incremental refinement, not first-time writes.
function.name: edit

file_path.description: Path to the file to modify

old_string.description: The exact text to find and replace

replace_all.description: If true, replace all occurrences. Default false.

function.description: Find files matching a glob pattern, sorted by modification time. Defaults to searching the input directory. Prefer this over `bash find` or `bash ls` for file discovery.
function.name: glob

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the input directory.

function.description: Search file contents using regex patterns. Defaults to searching the input directory. Returns matching file paths or matching lines with context.
function.name: grep

output_mode.description: Output format. 'content' shows matching lines, 'files_with_matches' shows file paths, 'count' shows match counts. Default: 'files_with_matches'.

path.description: File or directory to search in. Defaults to the input directory.
